News.title: ‘Black Widow’ carer is FINALLY jailed after keeping OAP like ‘caged animal’ & stealing £300k before fleeing to Tenerife
News.content:
AT LAST ‘Black Widow’ carer is FINALLY jailed after keeping OAP like ‘caged animal’ & stealing £300k before fleeing to Tenerife

A FRAUDSTER dubbed “the Black Widow” has finally been jailed after being hauled back to the UK from Tenerife to face justice.

Pamela Gwinnett fled the country to a Brit holiday hotspot where she hide for over a year before The Sun tracked her down.



Fuming locals described how she was sunbathing and relaxing in bars in her holiday island bolthole.

The twisted carer stole £300,000 from her “cash cow” Joan Greene and fled the country before she could be brought to justice.





She took up residence in her flat at a Brit tourist hotspot, with locals telling The Sun she spent her time sunbathing and drinking in bars.

The heartless 62-year-old, originally from Adlington, Cheshire, systematically plundered thousands from retired accountant Joan after setting herself up as the pensioner’s carer.

Gwinnett continued to steal money from Joan, 89, even after the pensioner passed away.

She was arrested for fraud by abuse of position and theft, but released on bail.



The carer applied for permission to fly to Tenerife, claiming she needed to scatter her brother’s ashes, which the court refused.

But five hours later, she was on a plane and fled the UK.



In her absence, the cruel monster was sentenced to six years in prison at Preston Crown Court – and the Judge Michael Maher called for help from the public and press to bring her back.

Video footage shows the moment she was escorted by GMP officers from the Terminal 3 arrival lounge at Manchester Airport into a police van.

Appearing in court today, a judge added two more months to her six year sentence.

Judge Michael Maher blasted: “You have treated this process as you did Joan Greene – with utter contempt”.



The judge, thanking the press for keeping the case in the public eye, blasted the twisted carer as “cowardly”.

He said the twisted carer had “continued to besmirch Joan’s family” from Tenerife.

The Sun previously revealed the fugitive was hiding in plain sight, flaunting her freedom by sunbathing and going to bars in Tenerife.



Fuming locals told The Sun they recognised Gwinnett from her mugshot – and are glad she has finally been dragged out, but wonder why it took so long.

One told The Sun: “It’s a small place, everyone knows everyone, and she’s always out and about.

“She’s very well known there.”

She was living in a penthouse apartment in a sunny town on the south-west coast of Tenerife, according to locals. It has since been locked up and the outside furniture taken in.

It is understood she also owns another apartment, which The Sun found on various holiday let websites priced at £112 a night – and it is booked solid until April.



The lavish seaside property has access to a pool, “stunning views”, a balcony, a big TV and a more than 8 out of 10 rating on a booking website.

But guests were seemingly cottoning on to who their host is – with some reviews naming “Pam” and one saying she is wanted by UK police.

The host responded by saying the post was “slander” – and said “get your facts right”.



One British pensioner told The Sun he met her in a bar, saying she tried to rent him a plush flat.

But later he discovered her “devious, evil crimes”.

The 66-year-old from Leeds said: “She’s certainly not hiding. I see her swanning about town, sometimes with some bloke – definitely British. It’s disgusting.

“She’s living off ill-gotten gains after robbing that sweet old lady of her dignity and her family.

“Spanish police need to pick her up. How is she allowed to just sunbathe all day? It’s abhorrent.”



Another raging pensioner told The Sun how Gwinnett appears “very pleasant and quite attractive” on the island.

She said Gwinnett had been visiting the area for a number of years, but moved there full-time in April.

“It’s terrible that she’s done that to that elderly lady who has since died, and she’s just pottering about freely.”

Others fumed that the wicked 62-year-old is “knocking around bars” looking “very glamorous” and “dolled up”.

Neighbours say they contacted the police demanding to know when Gwinnett would be hauled back to face justice.



The Black Widow owns a £200,000 red-brick house on a sleepy residential street in the leafy village of Adlington, Chorley, in Lancashire.

Those in the quiet northern town told The Sun they never expected her to be capable of such horrible acts.

Gwinnett seemingly hid her evil intentions behind a friendly façade, all the while keeping the vulnerable OAP caged like an animal at her home in Chorley.

Residents well remember her “midnight flit” as she fled the country last year.

Another neighbour, hopeful that the Black Widow would be caught and prosecuted, told us that Gwinnett “deserves what’s coming.”



The carer had claimed she was the grandmother’s carer but isolated frail, vulnerable Joan from her family.

She accused family members of mistreating the widow and did everything she could to keep them away while she fleeced her “golden goose.”

The carer spent money she stole from the “frail” 89-year-old on an Audi Q2, expensive meals, designer clothes, mortgages and Botox.

By the time Gwinnett’s power of attorney over Joan was suspended, she had already stolen £161,000 from the pensioner – and continued to do so after her death.

A court heard that the last months of Joan’s life had become “pock marked with increasing periods of bewilderment and confusion.”



The gran became doubly incontinent, but instead of looking after the elderly woman Gwinnett “bullied” her, the court was told.

In a heartbreaking video, Joan’s family are heard trying to comfort her while confronting Gwinnett.

Joan can be heard asking what is going on in the background, as grandson David reassures her: “People are looking out for you nan, people are looking out for you. We have your best interests at heart.”

Heartlessly, Gwinnett removes his hand from Joan’s and tells her: “Look at those lying eyes Joan.”

David is heard saying: “This is wrong. There’s only one person who is in the wrong. Give us a love nan. Love you. It’s alright.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joan’s step-daughter Katherine Farrimond, 65, said Joan believed in her final years that her family “hated her” and “didn’t want to see her” because of Gwinnett’s “lies”.

David previously told The Sun: “We were all disgusted – she’d used nan like a piggy bank.”

News.title: Mum who ‘couldn’t live without her kids’ took own life at pal’s home during custody row after becoming scared of arrest
News.content:
MUM'S HEARTBREAK Mum who ‘couldn’t live without her kids’ took own life at pal’s home during custody row after becoming scared of arrest

A MUM who “couldn’t live without her kids” tragically took her own life at her friend’s home during a custody battle, an inquest heard.

Nika Bittova, 44, was terrified that cops would arrest her during her job on the cosmetics counter at a branch of John Lewis.



The mum-of-three had seen a doctor about her low mood and told him: “I don’t want medication. I just want to see my children.”

A friend had also contacted her GP out of fears Nika “couldn’t go on living without them”.



She had been staying with her friend Laura Dielhenn after her 16-year relationship with the father of her children had broken down, the court heard.

Laura heartbreakingly found her friend lifeless at her home in Earley, Berkshire, on August 3 last year.



An inquest at Reading Coroner’s Court heard that Laura had been worried about her friend, who had told her the day before she was afraid the ongoing custody battle meant police would arrest her during her shift.

Although she had tried to reassure her that cops were unlikely to get involved in a family court case, Nika remained concerned.



At around 2am on August 3, Laura awoke to tend to her four-month-old baby and noticed the light was on in the room Nika was staying in.

When she went to sleep at around 4am, she noted the light was off.

Laura woke up at about 8am and an hour later knocked on her friend’s door to ask her if she wanted a cup of tea, but she got no answer and searched the house for her.

She rang Nika’s phone and heard it ringing in her room, where she sadly found her dead.

Police rushed to the home but she was pronounced dead at the scene.



The 44-year-old, who was originally from the Czech Republic, had worked as a sales representative at the Reading branch of John Lewis since November 2009.

She had been in a relationship with Michael Tiplady for 16 years, but the couple had split up and were amidst a custody battle, the coroner’s court heard.

The inquest was told Nika had not been able to see her family due to a court order.

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. It was also heard she had breached the conditions of her court order after visiting her daughter’s school in late 2024.

The mum-of-three had been staying with her friend Laura Dielhenn since January 2025 and had seen her doctor about low mood and anxiety.



In May 2025, she told a GP: “I don’t want medication. I just want to see my children.”

A friend had also contacted her doctor’s surgery to express concern after she had spoken about taking her own life.

She was recommended for counselling by her doctor, but the local NHS talking therapy team declined her request because she was already seeing a counsellor through a local mental health charity, the court heard.

In a tribute, Nika’s friend April Slater, said: “She was a brilliant, caring, girl and a great salesperson. She loved her children.

“She wanted to be back home with them. I saw how she had changed from the smiling, happy, girl she was.



“Nika felt she couldn’t go on living without them; without her children, there was no way out.”

Coroner Ian Wade said: “This is a sad and tragic death.

“I want to extend my sympathies and condolences to everyone who loved and cared for her.

“I would hope that anyone and everyone who has the opportunity to look after her children will make sure they continue to love their mother.”

News.title: Moment migrants chant ‘Allahu Akbar’ after ‘invading’ Spanish enclave as they clash with police on streets of Ceuta
News.content:
THIS is the moment migrants chant “Allahu Akbar” after allegedly invading the Spanish enclave of Ceuta before clashing with police.

Footage showed swarms of migrants shouting the phrase – which translates to “God is Great” – while holding an injured man who had reportedly been wounded by cops.



Spanish officers armed with batons were seen charging at crowds of men during the demonstration which erupted into violence on Sunday.

In the clip, a wounded man, who migrants claimed was assaulted by cops, is seen being carried away wrapped in a blanket.



Scores of men raising their fists haul him away from police as chants of “Allahu Akbar” ring out through the streets of Ceuta.

It came after some 60,000 people swam from Morocco into the Spanish city – located in North Africa – on Thursday.



Tens of thousands of migrants arrived in the Spanish territory – which shares a land border with Morocco – in just 24 hours.

Some of the migrants claimed Moroccan police encouraged them to cross the border into Spain.



Analysts have said that Morocco may have allowed migrants to cross the border to put diplomatic pressure on Spain.

Many Moroccans also said they were influenced by social media posts encouraging them to exploit a Spanish immigration loophole.

The African enclave endured days of chaos following the never-before-seen influx of migrants.



Jaw-dropping footage showed swarms of people running up the shores of Ceuta before pouring through the streets.

Terrified locals cowered in their homes as the streets turned into open toilets for hours in “apocalyptic” scenes.

Some migrants were heard shouting “Long live Spain!” as they dried off in the city.



One Spanish business owner told RTVE: “He said authorities had “no capacity” to control the chaos and that migrants are now bathing in public fountains and sleeping in the streets.

“It’s like an apocalypse. Waves of people everywhere.”

At least 72 people were killed due to drowning or the resulting beach stampede after the migrants crossed into the Spanish territory.

Most of those looking to breach the border swam around fences separating Ceuta from Morocco after seeing social media posts claiming they would be offered Spanish citizenship.



Suspected people smugglers have also been arrested after trying to sneak migrants into mainland Spain on jet skis and speedboats from Ceuta following the ordeal last week.

Shocking reports claim several locals suffered from attempted break-ins at their homes as footage captured multiple alleged incidents.

One shows a man climbing up a ladder as two others hold it still around what appears to be smashed glass from a first floor window.

A second seemingly shows dozens of migrants bundling into a small home and pushing through the tight entrance.



Spain’s government deployed hundreds of elite soldiers to take back control of the city as they sent the migrants to detention centres or escorted them back to Morocco.

Around 49,000 people voluntarily returned to Morocco after realising they wouldn’t gain citizenship and be allowed to stay safely according to Spanish officials.

Hundreds of migrants also tried to enter the Spanish territory of Melilla on the same day as the main Ceuta chaos.

France responded to the chaos near to Europe by tightening its borders in response to the deepening crisis and Italy suspended EU Schengen free-travel deal with Spain.

The Schengen agreement is a treaty that allows passport-free travel across 29 European countries.



The surge also sparked fears of further illegal migration into the UK.

Shadow Foreign Secretary Priti Patel has claimed some of those who made it into Ceuta would “inevitably try to make their way to the UK.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Reform leader Nigel Farage reacted to the border crisis by warning: “Thousands of young men, lots of them dangerous, will be heading towards Calais and our country. It’s time to wake up. This is a battle for our civilization.”

News.title: New hosepipe ban comes into force for 2MILLION people today with 14 more areas affected
News.content:
A NEW hosepipe ban has come into force for two million customers today with 14 new regions affected.

Brits continue to soak up the sun in parts of the UK today, with temperatures set to soar as high as 34C.

Essex and Suffolk Water has introduced a hosepipe ban from the early hours of this morning, as two million customers come under new restrictions.



It is the first time the water supplier has enforced a ban in nearly three decades, last seen back in June 1997.



Restrictions began at 0.01am this morning, but customers were encouraged to follow the rules from Friday, when it was announced.

The decision to introduce restrictions came as a result of “months of prolonged dry weather“, according to Essex and Suffolk Water.

A spokesperson said when the ban was announced: “July has seen little to no rainfall across East Anglia, with four successive heatwaves and the Environment Agency is starting to see more impact on the environment.

“Soils are extremely dry, affecting groundwater sources, river flows are low, and forecasts are for the hot and dry conditions to continue into August. ”

Full list of 14 new areas under hosepipe ban restrictions Essex: Barking

Basildon

Brentwood

Chelmsford

Hanningfield

Langford

Romford

Southend

Tilbury Suffolk: Barsham

Great Yarmouth

Lowestoft

Southwold

Walpole

Now, customers in 14 regions across Essex and Suffolk will be affected, including those in Southend, Chelmsford, Great Yarmouth, Romford, and more.

Both Anglian Water and Affinity Water already have hosepipe bans in place across Essex and Suffolk as a result of the dry conditions.



Under a temporary use ban, customers cannot use a hosepipe, sprinkler, or pressure washer for various activities, such as watering plants or filling up hot tubs.

Anyone caught breaking the rules can face a £1,000 fine, unless an approved exemption or loophole is in place.

Drought conditions continue to impact half of England and the entirety of Wales, with at least 23million under restrictions.

If your water supplier is affected, it is important to check their website to find out if your postcode has been affected by the temporary use ban.

News.title: X Factor finalist, 29, denies murdering influencer ‘dragged under car outside club amid ongoing dispute’
News.content:
AN X Factor finalist has denied murdering an influencer after allegedly driving into a crowd outside a club.

Gabrielle Carrington was arrested after three people were injured when a car struck them near the London Palladium in Soho.



The 29-year-old denied murder and GBH in court today after the horror in April.

Influencer Klaudia Zakrzewska – known as Klaudiaglam on Instagram – was rushed to hospital after being “dragged under” Carrington’s Mercedes.



The 32-year-old, from Essex, tragically died a week later after a desperate fight for life in hospital.

Security guard Anoush Chyche, aged in his 50s, was also reportedly struck by the car as he unlocked his e-scooter.



He was said to have suffered “life-changing injuries” when the car allegedly rolled over him.

Latisha Armstrong, aged in her 30s, was also struck and suffered a fractured bone in the wrist area.



A court previously heard there was reportedly an “ongoing dispute with the parties, and the parties were known to each other”.

Carrington appeared at the Old Bailey today via video-link from HMP Bronzefield wearing a black low cut top.

She denied murder and causing grievous bodily harm with intent and will face trial in January.

The singer was not asked to enter a plea to a third charge of driving with excess alcohol.

Carrington, from Manchester, first shot to fame as a teenager on The X Factor in 2013 as a member of girl group Miss Dynamix.



The popular act made it to the final of the competition with Carrington going on to become a TikTok and Instagram influencer with 362,000 followers online.

Prosecutor Rizwan Amin told the court previously: “In the early hours of Sunday morning 19 April, ambulances and police were called to Argyll Street for reports that a female had been run over.

“Officers had attended for 5am along with London ambulance service who were at the scene… it could only be described as a lot of people shouting.



“Many of the individuals who were there were from a nearby nightclub, including security members.”

The prosecutor said CCTV shows when Carrington arrived at Argyll Street in her car, “during this time she seems to have an altercation with a male”.

“She exited her car, this altercation had escalated to involve several other members of the public, and security tried to intervene to separate others involved.

“Ms Carrington was seen to return to the vehicle, which shows her immediately moving off and sharply mounting a pavement.

“During this manoeuvre the vehicle had struck Ms Klaudia, who was positioned on the front side of the vehicle, and was trapped and dragged under the vehicle.”



He added as the vehicle moved forward it struck a security guard who was on the pavement.

“At this point the vehicle couldn’t move any further and Ms Carrington then reversed a short distance, causing it to roll over Mr Anoush Chyche.

“During this manoeuvre Ms Letisha Armstrong was also hit by the vehicle and suffered a fractured bone in the wrist area.”

Klaudia’s heartbroken family previously spoke of how they spent a week keeping vigil by her hospital bedside in a “living hell” before she died.



They told The Sun she was declared “brain dead” after the horrific incident.

A close family member told us that Klaudia’s “kindly heart” had been slowing down and her “organs failing”.

They added: “Klaudia touched many hearts and we are all in agony.”

Klaudia’s mum previously posted a message with an image of her daughter in a desert wearing a beige dress, she said: “I am asking from the deepest place in my heart – please keep my beautiful daughter Klaudia in your prayers right now.



“She is my angel, my world, my everything, and she needs all the love, strength, and healing we can send her.

“Please lift her up in your prayers – for comfort, protection, and strength during this difficult time. Your love and support mean more to me than words can express.

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart. (heart emoji) Klaudia’s Mum (heart emoji).”

A GoFundMe was set up by Klaudia’s relatives, with her mum describing it as the “most devastating time” the family has faced.

She wrote: “As many of you may already know, my daughter is currently in a coma and desperately fighting for her life.



“Those who know me understand how much I love my daughter and what a special bond we have, and I cannot give up on my baby girl.

“Klaudia is in critical condition, and due to the severity of her injuries, doctors do not believe she will survive.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am deeply grateful to everyone who has already helped us during this incredibly painful time.

“Your kindness, prayers, and support mean more than words can express.”

News.title: Woman in her 30s ‘raped’ in house on residential street – as five men arrested
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

HORROR ATTACK Woman in her 30s ‘raped’ in house on residential street – as five men arrested

COPS have arrested five men on suspicion of rape after a woman in her 30s was allegedly attacked in a house.

Police launched an urgent investigation after reports of the “serious sexual assault” at a property on Curriers Lane in Ipswich, in the early hours of the morning on Sunday.

Five men, aged 27, 31, 35, 44 and 49, were arrested on suspicion of rape, Suffolk Police confirmed.

They are currently in police custody for questioning.





The woman is being supported by specialist trained officers, said cops.

Suffolk Police said that a crime scene was in place at Curriers Lane.

There will be an “increased police presence” in the area as the investigation continues, the force added.

Suffolk Police urged anyone with information to get in touch immediately.

Detective Chief Inspector Craig Brett said: “I understand the concern this may cause the local community and would like to assure the public that our teams have been working tirelessly since the incident was reported to us.

“A scene remains in place on Curriers Lane and there is currently an increased police presence in the area as we conduct our enquiries to establish the full circumstances surrounding this incident.

“We encourage the public to speak with officers if you have any concerns or information.”

Anyone with information relating to the incident can also contact police quoting 37/45328/26 via the Suffolk Police website or call 101.



Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers 100% anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their online form.

News.title: Couple locked in 14-year neighbour battle over fence, ornamental squirrel & offensive YouTube songs ordered to pay £150k
News.content:
A COUPLE who have been locked in a 14-year-long row over a fence stole the neighbour’s ornamental squirrel and released explicit songs about them on YouTube.

Philip New, 52, and his wife Denise, 47, now face a £150,000 court bill after a small disagreement about a fence being a few inches out of line escalated into an all-out war.



The pair were sued by their neighbours Steve and Karen Gibson who said the fence row has caused them distress and even reduced them to tears.

Mr Gibson told the court of his upset when Mr New removed an ornamental squirrel from a post between the properties shortly after they lost an appeal in the case.



The builder was also shocked to learn that comedy songwriter Mr New had written and published derogatory songs about him and the battle between the two couples on YouTube.

One song, titled Neighbours, purported to offer advice on how to deal with bad neighbours and included the words: “Throw sh*t at their window, sh*t at the door/ Call him a w****r, call her a w***e.”



After a judge found against Mr and Mrs New at Southend County Court last year, they were ordered to pay the Gibsons £13,305 in combined damages and interest, and handed lawyers’ bills estimated at about £120,000 for the case.

However, they launched a High Court appeal against the damages amount, arguing that it was substantially too high and should be reduced, with the result that the costs bill should also be overturned.



The court ruled on Friday to reduce the damages amount by £700, but the News have instead been handed a further £19,000 bill for their neighbours’ legal costs after a judge found the Gibsons were the winners of the case in “substance and reality”.

Mr Justice Thompsell said the News’ motivation for appealing had been to secure a big enough reduction in the damages to allow them to avoid having to pay their neighbours’ costs.

However, he said a £700 reduction did not justify overturning the six-figure bill they were already facing, and ordered them to pay on top of that the Gibsons’ near £19,000 costs of the appeal.

In the earlier judgment at the county court, Judge Robert Duddridge described the “wretched” dispute as one which had “consumed” the neighbours’ lives and was “unusually disproportionate, difficult and frustrating.”

Setting out the background, he said the two couples live in next door semi-detached properties in Sunnymede Close, Thundersley, Essex, with their gardens separated by a wooden fence.



The dispute began in 2012 when Mr New replaced some fence panels, with the Gibsons complaining that it was in the wrong place and not in a straight line.

The couples agreed to settle their differences outside court, with the appointment of an independent surveyor to determine the line of the boundary in 2015.

But Mr and Mrs New disagreed with the line chosen by the expert and had a second opinion by another, leading to the dispute escalating into a court battle when the Gibsons sued in 2018.



In 2021, the court ruled on the case, resulting in a declaration that the line chosen by the first surveyor had to be abided by and handing victory to Mr and Mrs Gibson.

After a series of failed appeals, the case then moved on to Judge Duddridge for a determination of the amount in damages which the Gibsons were due for the News’ fence having trespassed on their land.

In his evidence, Mr Gibson, who has a rare disability affecting his bones, said he thought the 2015 agreement would bring “finality” to the dispute but instead the News had not accepted it and continued to trespass.

Interactions with their neighbours became “hostile” and they no longer used their garden like they would have done otherwise, he claimed.

He said he had “lost his heart and soul” and he and his wife had been moved to tears at times due to the conflict with Mr and Mrs New.



He told the court of his upset when Mr New removed an ornamental squirrel from a post between the properties shortly after they lost an appeal in the case, before then removing the post itself with his hands and a mallet.

“According to his statement, the squirrel post had been built by his parents in law after he purchased the squirrel as a gift for Mrs Gibson and her parents during the 1980s and, for that reason, it had enormous sentimental value,” said the judge.

Mr New argued he removed the squirrel post because it was dangerous but this was rejected by Judge Duddridge.

In November 2020, one of the Gibsons’ children had discovered two songs – titled ‘Neighbours’ and ‘Magic Garden’ – on YouTube and Facebook, said the judge.

“The song ‘Neighbours’ gives advice to the listener about how to deal with bad neighbours, including: ‘Throw shi*t at their window, sh*t at the door/ Call him a w***er, call her a w***e/ P*ss in their garden, till it’s quite late/ When they’re asleep, blow up their gate’,” he said.



“The song ‘Magic Garden’ describes somebody who uses walking sticks and purports to be in pain when out in public, but throws their sticks away and is miraculously pain free when in their garden and is committing benefits fraud.

“Mr Gibson described how upsetting, hurtful and hateful he found this song, which he thought was clearly about him, in view of his serious and rare disability and the difficulties he has had coming to terms with it.”

While the judge did not think the News’ would carry out the song’s advice he said: “I am satisfied that the songs ‘Neighbours’ and ‘Magic Garden’ were directly about the Gibsons.”

Mr New could have foreseen that uploading the song to social media means they might have been seen by people who know the Gibsons.

“As he ended up acknowledging, their content is offensive and defamatory. I accept that the claimants, in particular Mr Gibson, found the songs deeply hurtful and embarrassing given his rare condition, and that it aggravated the unpleasantness, emotional upset and mental health issues caused by this dispute.”



Although the fence only trespassed by a “matter of inches,” the Gibsons were “entitled to be compensated for the inconvenience and distress” they were caused.

They were awarded “aggravated damages” due to Mr and Mrs New’s “high-handed, insulting or oppressive conduct.”

When the case appeared before the High Court, the judge ordered a £700 reduction in the overall amount to be paid on the basis that the lower judge may have wrongly awarded damages for a period after the end of 2021 when the Gibsons could have erected a new fence.

However, the judge refused to cut the damages in reference to the squirrel post incidents and the explicit songs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The previous judge “was assessing damages for distress, loss of privacy, inconvenience and loss of amenity caused by both a continuing trespass and a breach of an agreement and found justification for doing this in a number of decided cases,” he added.



The decision means Mr and Mrs New will have to pay their neighbours about £12,600 in damages, nearly £19,000 to cover their lawyers’ bills for the appeal, and also to foot the bill for the proceedings at the county court, estimated by the Gibsons’ legal team at about £120,000.

News.title: Brit dad arrested over death of son, 2, who fell from Cyprus window breaks down as he’s allowed to fly to UK for funeral
News.content:
A BRITISH city exec whose toddler died after falling from a fourth-floor window at a Cyprus hotel has been allowed to go home for the two-year-old boy’s funeral.

The 37-year-old, from a village near Essex, was barred from leaving the Mediterranean island after he was charged with causing death by a rash, reckless or dangerous act.



The Brit, 37, spent eight days in jail after his arrest and was forced to tell his young girl about the tragedy over FaceTime.

A Cypriot judge initially bailed him in exchange for 20,000 euros (£17,000), but took his passport and banned him from travelling home.



At Paphos district court today Judge Froso Christodoulidou lifted the travel restrictions between August 5 and September 14.

The father, who works at a big four consultancy firm, has been ordered to pay an additional 10,000 euros (£8,500) deposit to ensure his return for the beginning of the trial on September 17.



Holding back tears after the hearing, the Brit said: “I’m very thankful to the judge and to the authorities for letting me go home to my wife and my daughter.

“That’s all I want to do now.”

Alexandros Alexandrou, defending, said: “Today he is still struggling, but he is happy with this outcome.

“He was crying because, as we all understand, he needs to go back to his family, to his house, to grieve properly and to reunite with the members of the family – not only with his wife.



“Today for him is a good day, it is a nice day because he was thinking they would not allow him to travel back and attend the funeral.

“If this would happen it would have been a disaster for him – devastating.”

The young boy’s body was returned to the UK last week, while the father’s parents stayed in Cyprus to support him.



The horror fall happened just hours after the family arrived on the sunny island on July 12 for their summer holiday at the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort.

How the little boy fell to his death is disputed, with the dad saying that he sat his child on a window ledge next to an elevator while waiting to go to the dinner in the hotel restaurant.

The banker’s parents consoled him in Paphos district court on Friday morning as he sat with his head bowed before his case was called, dressed in a white shirt and navy blue trousers.

The horror fall happened just hours after the family arrived on the sunny island for their summer holiday.

How the little boy fell to his death is disputed, with the dad saying that he sat his child on a window ledge next to an elevator while waiting to go to the dinner in the hotel restaurant.



Last week the court heard that he was swinging his son from side to side before the fall, but it is understood that the suspect denies this.

Investigators have said they think the Brit could have been unaware that the window was open.

The Sun has seen the 4ft wide, 8ft tall sliding window from where the tot fell and can confirm that it can still easily be opened.

If convicted, the city exec could face up to four years in prison.

Last week, a friend of the family paid tribute to the child – whose body was returned to the UK on Wednesday – describing him as a “truly special, easy-going little boy who brought joy to everyone around him.



They added: “He was deeply adored and his infectious smile, warm cuddles and kind heart are already so deeply missed and always will be.”

The resort’s safety record has come under scrutiny after it emerged that the toddler is the third British tourist to die there since 2022.

Ben Woods, 21, from Leigh in Greater Manchester drowned while playing in the hotel pool in July 2022.

And six-year-old Ruaridh Nairne, from Inverness, drowned there in 2024.

Antonis Sivitanidis, general manager of the King Evelthon hotel, said: “Allegations made by guests [on health and safety] I will not comment on as everyone has their own opinion.



“Our hotel is fully licensed and complies with all regulations. It is safe for visitors to come and stay.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are very sorry for all the families involved and we offer them our sincere condolences and sympathy.”

The trial is due to continue on September 17 where the Brit is expected to enter a guilty or not guilty plea.

News.title: Nigel Farage – live: Reform UK leader breaks cover after weeks of finances questions as Richard Tice probed
News.content:
Nigel Farage will break cover to hold a press conference at 11am today - it will be the first one in London held by the Reform UK leader for months, and comes amid ongoing questions about his finances

Under-pressure Nigel Farage will break cover to hold a press conference at 11am today.

It will be the first London press conference held by the Reform UK leader for months. Mr Farage has been laying low since he last month dramatically quit as the MP for Clacton to trigger a by-election in the area.

This time last year, Reform UK was holding weekly press conferences over the summer. But in recent months, as pressure grows over Mr Farage's finances, the party has scurried away from scrutiny.

A standards investigation into Mr Farage's failure to declare a £5million gift from Thai-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has been paused since he quit as an MP. It will be restarted if he is re-elected as an MP in next week's Clacton by-election.

Follow live updates below...

News.title: Jet2 passenger stopped by customs at UK airport shouts 'get in there' after avoiding prison
News.content:
Jet2 passenger stopped by customs at UK airport shouts 'get in there' after avoiding prison

Paul Barrett was found to have cannabis and ketamine in a suitcase by customs officers after landing at Newcastle Airport on a Jet2 flight from Faro

View Image Paul Barrett tried to bring in drugs to Newcastle Airport (Image: Police Handout)

A man shouted "get in there" when he learned he had avoided prison after being caught with 20kg of cannabis at an airport.

‌



Former soldier Paul Barrett was found to have cannabis and a kilogram of ketamine when he was stopped by customs officers as he collected luggage from the carousel at Newcastle Airport, after arriving on a Jet2 from Faro on May 4.

‌



When challenged, Barrett, who has previous convictions including possessing cocaine with intent to supply, confessed he had "some weed" and said he had racked up debts from cocaine and gambling addictions.

‌



He was given a suspended prison sentence at Newcastle Crown Court and after politely assuring a judge he wouldn't let him down, he let out a celebratory outburst.

UK weather maps show 7C morning chill with 40 areas below 10C – full list READ MORE :

Neil Jones, prosecuting, said: "He confirmed he was a solo traveller and all of the bags were his own. Asked if he had packed them, he said he had not packed the suitcase, which had been given to him. Asked about its contents, he said 'I'm going to be honest with you, I'm carrying some weed. I've got a debt I owe."

Inside the case, customs officers found four packages which contained 20.5kg of cannabis resin and another package with 1.12kg of ketamine. The wholesale value of the drugs was £80,000 but they would have been worth much more when broken down into deals.

‌



Barrett gave a prepared statement saying he was an army veteran who had PTSD and he said he had cocaine and gambling addictions which had taken hold of him since he left the army, reported ChronicleLive.

Barrett has 18 previous convictions, including for possessing cocaine with intent to supply, for which he got a suspended sentence in 2023. He also has convictions for being concerned in the supply of ketamine, possessing cocaine and drug driving.

For the latest offending, the 38-year-old, from Ormskirk, Lancashire, pleaded guilty to two counts of being concerned in the fraudulent evasion on the prohibition on the importation of cannabis and ketamine.

‌



Chris Knox, defending, said: "He understands what a mess he has made by getting involved in drugs. He very much gets the message and he understands almost all of his difficulties in relation to the courts have arisen from his involvement with drugs.

"He is desperate to get back to the care of his children and he has a job offer and the employment involves him being subjected to drug tests."

Judge Sarah Mallet told Barrett she would give him "one last chance" and sentenced him to 18 months suspended for two years with 100 hours of unpaid work.

Article continues below

Barrett, appearing in court on a video-link from prison, said: "Thank your for the opportunity ma'am and I won't let you down. I'm thinking of my children."

After being told he would be released, he was heard shouting "get in there" as he left the video-link room.

News.title: X Factor finalist denies murdering influencer Klaudiaglam with car outside Soho nightclub
News.content:
X Factor finalist denies murdering influencer Klaudiaglam with car outside Soho nightclub

Gabrielle Carrington, 29, has denied murdering Klaudia Zakrzewska, who died six days after an incident outside the Inca nightclub in Argyll Street, Soho, in the early hours of April 19

View 3 Images Klaudia Zakrzewska, a TikTok and Instagram influencer who went by the name Klaudiaglam, died on April 25 (Image: klaudiaglam/Instagram)

A former X Factor finalist has denied murdering a social media influencer by running her over with a car in central London.

Gabrielle Carrington, 29, allegedly struck Klaudia Zakrzewska, 32, outside the Inca nightclub in Argyll Street, Soho, at 4.30am on April 19.

Carrington, of Broadfield Road, Manchester, was initially charged with attempted murder, but that was changed to murder after Ms Zakrzewska died from her injuries on April 25.

On Monday, Carrington appeared at the Old Bailey via videolink from Bronzefield prison. The defendant was not represented by a barrister and represented herself during the plea hearing.

View 3 Images Defendant Gabrielle Carrington made it to the X Factor live finals in 2013 as a member of the trio Miss Dynamix (Image: PA)

Asked if she was happy to proceed without a lawyer, Carrington told Judge Sarah Whitehouse KC that she did not want to represent herself "for the foreseeable". But she added: "As I’m not represented, I am happy to give a plea today even though I am not represented."

Carrington pleaded not guilty to murder and a second charge of causing grievous bodily harm with intent to security guard Anoush Chyche. The defendant was not asked to enter a plea to a third charge of driving with excess alcohol.

On her decision over who would ultimately represent her at her trial, she said: "This is my life. This is the toughest decision I have to make."

Judge Whitehouse confirmed she would try the case at the Old Bailey from January 5. She set a further pre-trial hearing for August 11 and October 9.

The defendant interacted directly with the judge and prosecutor Crispin Aylett KC during the hearing and made notes on a large pad of paper.

Judge Whitehouse remanded her into custody but ordered that she be brought to the Old Bailey for her next hearing.

It is alleged that Carrington had arrived in Argyll Street in her car and had appeared to have a row with a man as she got out of the vehicle. The altercation escalated as more people became involved, prompting security staff to intervene.

View 3 Images Court artist sketch of Gabrielle Carrington appearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court on April 21 (Image: Elizabeth Cook/PA Wire)

Carrington allegedly got back into the car and moved off, sharply mounting the pavement, striking Ms Zakrzewska. The vehicle went on to strike a security member of staff, Mr Chyche, who was on the pavement, it is claimed.

As it reversed, Ms Zakrzewska could be seen underneath the vehicle, lying prone on the ground.

At 5am, paramedics and police attended the scene and found people shouting, many of whom had left the nearby Inca nightclub. Ms Zakrzewska died later in hospital, while Mr Chyche, in his 50s, suffered "life-changing injuries".

According to the court charges, Carrington had 61 microgrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath when she tested after the incident.

The defendant, who has more than 365,000 followers on Instagram under the handle RIELLEUK, made it to the X Factor live finals in 2013 as one of the three members of Miss Dynamix. She is described in court as a "social media influencer" who makes regular trips to the United Arab Emirates.

Article continues below

Ms Zakrzewska was a TikTok and Instagram influencer who went by the name Klaudiaglam.

News.title: 'I would order three bottles of wine off Deliveroo every night - then I had a spiritual awakening'
News.content:
'I would order three bottles of wine off Deliveroo every night - then I had a spiritual awakening'

Karen Gray says drinking used to be her 'hobby' and she would plan it around when she was looking after her daughter

View 4 Images Karen Gray, 53, struggled to say no to a night out from a young age and described getting drunk as her main 'hobby' (Image: SWNS)

A mum who would drink two bottles of wine every night and had weekend benders while her young daughter was at her dad's is celebrating six years sober. Karen Gray, 53, struggled to say no to a night out from a young age and described getting drunk as her main “hobby”.

‌



The photographer, from Swindon, was able to give up drinking when she got pregnant with her daughter Sophie, now 20, but started again soon after she gave birth, leading to her splitting up with Sophie’s father.

‌



Karen would drink two bottles of wine every night of the week, and planned her drinking around when Sophie was at her dad's house. She said lockdown caused her drinking to escalate, and she used Deliveroo to order bottles of wine to her house, before attempting to take her own life in April 2020.

‌



Karen was found by her friend and blue-lighted to the hospital, where she had a "spiritual awakening" and is now celebrating six years sober. The mum of one said: “When I used to drink, I would drink to the point where I couldn’t stop.

View 4 Images Karen would order endless bottles of wine off Deliveroo (Image: SWNS)

“I’d have one, then want another one, and then another one. I couldn’t just have one glass of wine; I’d have the whole bottle. My hobby was going out and getting drunk; I would do it at any opportunity.

‌



“My whole life was built around when I could drink next. I feel like a completely different person now; I’m so at peace. My daughter and I have always been best friends, but now I can finally connect with her properly.”

Karen’s first experience of alcohol was when she was 16 and still in school. She would go to house parties at the weekend, and then, when she was 17, she started going out to local pubs and bars.

“Every time I went out drinking, I’d get in trouble with the police for just being mouthy and gobby," Karen said. “I got barred from every single pub in my local town at age 19, but I saw it as a badge of honour.”

‌



Mum sheds more than one third of her bodyweight after daughter's desperate plea READ MORE :

As she got a bit older, Karen started frequenting the London clubbing scene, where she would take ecstasy every weekend. “I was changing the way I felt because I was uncomfortable in my own skin," she said.

At age 25, Karen got a job working for the local council and would drink a bottle or two of wine by herself in her flat every night after work. She said: “I would be on a bender from Friday to Sunday, and then I wouldn’t go to work on the Monday. The number of Mondays I had off from that job was unreal.”

When Karen was 34, in 2004, she became pregnant with her daughter Sophie and decided she needed to “sort my life out”. She stopped drinking during her pregnancy and for the first three months after Sophie’s birth, until one day in March, 2005, she met up with a girl from her clubbing days and ended up getting “smashed” in the middle of the afternoon.

‌



Karen said: “That was me back to wanting to drink every night. I’d always said to myself that if I had a child, I would stop. That’s when I knew I had a serious problem.”

View 4 Images Karen used to drink heavily from a young age (Image: SWNS)

Sophie’s dad ended up looking after his young daughter a lot whilst Karen was drinking. The couple split in 2007, when Sophie was two years old, due to Karen’s drinking.

‌



After the breakdown of their relationship, Karen would plan nights out at weekends and on Wednesdays, when Sophie was at her dad’s house. Realising she needed to make a serious change, Karen checked into rehab for a month in 2007 to try and kick her habit for good.

“That’s where I learned that addiction is a disease," she said. Karen began going to recovery meetings and started the 12-step program, but says she didn’t take it seriously.

She said: “I wanted to do things my way, and I would just pick and choose bits of the programme."

‌



After two years of sobriety, Karen relapsed in 2009. “As soon as I picked up that drink, it was back to square one," she said. After relapsing, Karen was back to drinking two bottles of wine on Wednesday's and at the weekend whilst Sophie was at her dad's.

Karen said: “I felt like I was a rubbish mum and I was doing everything wrong, even though I loved my daughter so much. The guilt that came after I’d had a heavy session drinking was just awful.”

View 4 Images Karen (left) with daughter Sophie (Image: SWNS)

‌



When lockdown hit in 2020, Karen’s drinking escalated due to her fears around the pandemic. "As soon as Boris came on the TV at 5pm, I'd crack open a bottle of wine," she said.

This led to her attempting to take her own life in April 2020. While she was in hospital, Karen had an “internal click” and realised she did not want to continue living life this way.

“I’ve not wanted to pick up a drink since that day," she said. “Not once."

Article continues below

She went back to recovery meetings and got a sponsor to help her through the 12-step programme. “I felt like lockdown was my own private little rehab, because no one was going out and partying, so I didn’t feel like I was missing out on anything," she said.

She started her recovery programme on Zoom before going to meetings in person when lockdown restrictions lifted. Karen has now been sober for six years and says she feels like she has had a “spiritual awakening”.

In 2024, she was diagnosed with ADHD, which she believes fed into her struggles with addiction. Karen said: “As soon as I started taking the medication, I felt so much calmer, and it got rid of my anxiety. I wish I had been diagnosed when I was younger; things may have been so different."

News.title: Richard Tice faces standards probe over 'failure to declare an interest'
News.content:
Richard Tice faces standards probe over 'failure to declare an interest'

Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice is under investigation by the standards commissioner over a failure to declare an interest, it has emerged today

View 2 Images Richard Tice is Reform UK's deputy leader (Image: PA)

Richard Tice is under investigation by the standards commissioner over an alleged failure to declare an interest.

‌



The deputy Reform UK leader faces a probe as his boss Nigel Farage comes under mounting pressure over his finances.

‌



It's understood the probe into Mr Tice relates to the declaration of an interest in Israel when speaking on antisemitism in Westminster hall. The investigation was opened on July 28.

‌



In a statement posted on X, Mr Tice said: "I am being investigated for standing against antisemitism. You could not make it up. Standards Commissioner is considering complaint by anti semitic anti Israel lobby group over whether I should have referenced my register of interests at start of a debate on UK democracy and Israeli influence.

View 2 Images A standards investigation into Nigel Farage's failure to declare a £5million gift from Thai-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne was paused when he quit as an MP (Image: James Veysey/Shutterstock)

‌



"The same anti Israel group failed to notify Commissioner that Ayoub Khan MP did not declare his substantial donation received from a pro Palestine group."

A standards investigation into Mr Farage's failure to declare a £5million gift from Thai-based cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne was paused when he quit as an MP. It will be restarted if he is re-elected as an MP in next week's Clacton by-election.

Reform has long insisted the £5million gift was a personal, unconditional gift, meaning there was no need to declare it.

Article continues below

Standards Commissioner Daniel Greenberg was looking into whether Mr Farage broke Parliamentary rules requiring new MPs are to declare any potentially relevant gifts or donations received in the 12 months before they enter the Commons.

The £5million was given to Mr Farage by Mr Harborne shortly before he announced he was standing in the Clacton constituency in 2024.

News.title: NOW TV Licence rules as UK households could be hit with £1k fine
News.content:
NOW TV Licence rules as UK households could be hit with £1k fine

The fine is a hefty one - and one that can easily be avoided

View 3 Images You can submit a “No Licence Needed” declaration (Image: Getty)

A TV Licence costs £180 and gives you legal access to a range of channels and live broadcasts, but it isn’t only the BBC that requires one. Now (previously Now TV) is a Sky-owned, subscription TV service that offers contract-free access to Sky’s premium sports, movies and entertainment, as explained by Which?

‌



NOW confirms: "You’ll need a TV licence if you watch any of the live channels with your NOW Membership, on any device." It adds: "You’ll also need a TV licence if you use your NOW Box or Smart Stick to watch BBC iPlayer (live programmes, on demand or catch up)."

‌



How much is a TV Licence fine?

View 3 Images The fee increased in April 2026 (Image: Getty)

‌



A standard TV Licence costs £180 and a black and white licence costs £60.50. TV Licensing confirms: "You could be prosecuted if we find that you have been watching, recording or downloading programmes illegally.

"The maximum penalty is a £1,000 fine plus any legal costs and/or compensation you may be ordered to pay. The maximum fine is £2,000 in Guernsey."

‌



This means if you don't have a TV Licence but watch live channels with your NOW Membership, for example, you could be handed a £1,000 fine.

How much is NOW?

View 3 Images People may need a TV Licence and not know it (Image: Getty)

A NOW membership lets you watch what you want, when it suits you. You can sign up to Entertainment, Cinema or Sports, and get access to live TV channels as well as on-demand content. Prices vary with offers available for some.
