News.title: 'Two words' Royal Mail customers need to write on back of every letter
News.content:
'Two words' Royal Mail customers need to write on back of every letter

Royal Mail urges customers to include the words to help ensure the post gets to its final destination

View 3 Images The tip could be helpful for anyone sending post in the mail (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

Royal Mail customers are advised to write two important words on every parcel or letter they send. The postal service provides advice on its website to help customers ensure their mail reaches its destination as quickly as possible.

‌



The advice includes tips on how to address an envelope so it can be delivered to the right place. Customers are also asked to add a return address to anything they send in the post, in case the item can't be delivered.

‌



As Royal Mail's website explains, all customers should write 'return address' on the back of the envelope, followed by their information. Taking a few seconds to add the information could be vital if there's an unexpected issue during delivery.

‌



The postal service said: "If for any reason your item can't be delivered, we can send it back to you. Write the words 'return address' on the back of the envelope and underneath that, the actual return address." In the illustrative photo shared alongside the advice, Royal Mail wrote the return address on the bottom right of the envelope.

Customers should make sure that both the send and return addresses are clearly visible and easy to read. Royal Mail said: "It's important that the address shows up against the colour of your envelope."

View 3 Images Royal Mail customers can view the advice online (Image: Getty)

‌



If customers are using a coloured envelope, it could be helpful to use a white label on the address side. Royal Mail suggests using black ink. Royal Mail's website also explains how to address the envelope, providing specific guidance for different countries, as the required format may vary.

Generally, Royal Mail said the top line should be the recipient's full name. The middle lines are used for the person's specific address.

Royal Mail explained: "Use a line for the property number and street name. If the property has a full name, this can take up one line and drop the street name onto the next line.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Customers are advised to add a return address to post (Image: Getty)

"On the following line, you can put the name of the local area or village name. Next, write the name of the town in capital letters. You don't need to include a county name, as your letters and parcels will still reach the right place. However, you can include it if you prefer."

Finally, the bottom line should be the UK postcode or information about the international destination. Royal Mail said: "UK destination: The final line should be the UK postcode, again in capital letters. International destination: After the area code, add the country name to the final line, again in capital letters."

News.title: Brit pilot SURVIVES after helicopters crash mid-air while battling Greek wildfires
News.content:
Brit pilot SURVIVES after helicopters crash mid-air while battling Greek wildfires

Two aircrafts helping put out the horror wildfires in Greece smashed into each other mid-air - two people died but a British pilot was among the survivors

View 4 Images Moment two helicopters crashed mid-air in Greece

A British pilot survived a horror fireball crash in Greece after two helicopters tackling wildfires smashed into each other mid-air.

‌



The horror collision, on Sunday, left two crew members dead as terrifying footage caught the moment the helicopters slammed into one another. A Danish pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer were tragically killed in the blaze and they were the only people on one of the choppers.

‌



A British pilot and a Greek crew member on the other helicopter survived the crash. Footage caught the two helicopters slowly crossing paths while at low altitude over the wildfires, in Psatha, west of Athens.

‌



UK wildfires cause devastation to rare wildlife habitats that could take 25 years to recover READ MORE :

View 4 Images One helicopter plunged to the ground after the collision

One of the helicopters was seen clipping the rotary blades of the other before it exploded and plunged into a ravine. The second aircraft made an emergency landing.

The Greek Fire Service said two Bell helicopters, which had been leased from Australian company McDermott Aviation, collided while trying to put out a huge wildfire that had been raging on the Attica-Boeotia border.

‌



A Greek civil protection ministry source, according to the BBC, allegedly said: "The two people on board, a British pilot and a Greek fire service liaison officer - escaped with minor injuries. Both remained conscious and have been admitted to hospital, where they will remain under observation for 24 hours as a precaution."

View 4 Images Smoke rising from a mountain where the aircraft crashed (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Greece's fire ⁠department in a statement after the deadly crash said: "During the aerial firefighting operation, two BELL helicopters, leased by the fire department, with a crew of two people each, crashed in the wider area of Psatha, Attica. The helicopters had taken off from the Elefsina military airport. The search and rescue operation is under way." This source also claimed the British pilot was not part of an exchange between Greece and the UK but was a hired privately.

‌



Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, in a post on X, said: "I express my deepest sorrow for the tragic accident involving the two leased firefighting helicopters that cost the lives of two frontline fighters in the war against the fires under highly adverse weather conditions—especially for our aerial assets. The loss of the Greek coordinator and the Danish pilot while they were operating in the major fire at Porto Germeno fills us all with grief. Sincere condolences to their families."

View 4 Images Firefighters at the site where the helicopter crashed (Image: STRINGER/EPA/Shutterstock)

Article continues below

This comes after winds drove flames deeper into the Athens region on Sunday and forced a new wave of evacuations. Fires spread through western Attica, the region around Athens, and threatened communities and an industrial district outside Megara as violent gusts stopped firefighting aircraft from collecting water from the sea.

Athens has not been the only area in Greece battling horror wildfires as flames threatened homes on Kefalonia, forcing evacuations from inland communities as aircraft made water drops over the island. Firefighters battled another blaze near Nea Tenedos in Halkidiki.

Two firefighters died battling a fire on Crete earlier this week, while a third was killed in a separate fire in the Peloponnese. Wildfires have also ravaged Spain and 224,000 were forced to flee their homes in France.

News.title: English FA set to withdraw support for Fifa president Infantino
News.content:
The English Football Association is set to write to Fifa president Gianni Infantino withdrawing its support amid the fallout from his scrapped plans to sell off stakes in Fifa competitions to private investors.

It comes as Uefa threatens legal action over the proposals and Wales publicly withdraw backing for Infantino's bid to continue as Fifa president.

Infantino's leadership had already been publicly questioned by football's governing bodies in Europe, North and Central America and the Caribbean, with Uefa and Concacaf releasing statements criticising the plans.

Fifa and Infantino wanted to create a commercial subsidiary to run its main events, including its World Cups, and external investors would have been able to buy stakes in it.

World football's governing body said it would "invite third parties to make minority, non-controlling investments" in a new subsidiary called Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE).

As first reported by The Telegraph, Uefa said in a letter to Infantino "it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the 'proceedings') arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa".

Uefa added it wants "immediate steps to identify, locate and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa possession, custody or control.

"These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply."

BBC Sport has approached Fifa for comment.

News.title: Teacher has ground-breaking surgery while pregnant to treat baby's intestinal defect
News.content:
Doctors have used ground-breaking surgery on an unborn baby to successfully correct a birth defect while he was still inside the womb.

His mother, Maisie Savage, from London, was operated on by doctors in the US while she was 26 weeks pregnant.

Baby Theo, who is now five months old and thriving, had gastroschisis, where the belly button does not develop properly, causing the intestines to grow externally.

Doctors partially exposed his mother's womb and then gently pushed his organs back inside his abdomen using keyhole surgery.

He was the third baby in the world to benefit from the first-of-its-kind clinical trial.

Maisie, 29, and Theo's father, Josh French, 36, both teachers, say they are incredibly relieved by the success of the pioneering surgery.

"He's a little miracle, isn't he?" Maisie told BBC News.

But they both know things could have been very different.

The serious birth defect affects one in 3,000 UK babies each year. In the best-case scenarios, babies can require weeks in intensive care and nutritional feeding through a tube or IV and corrective surgery.

For the most complex cases, like Theo's, outcomes are far more serious with up to six months in neonatal intensive care, multiple surgeries, IV nutritional feeding for up to two years, and a possible intestinal transplant.

Even with the highest level of medical care, one in 10 babies will die.

News.title: Reform UK's Richard Tice investigated by parliamentary standards watchdog
News.content:
Reform UK's deputy leader Richard Tice is being investigated by the parliamentary standards watchdog over an allegation he failed to declare an interest.

The investigation was opened on Tuesday 28 July and was published on the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner website on Monday.

Tice said the complaint related to a Commons debate about Israeli influence and whether he should had referenced his register of interests. Reform said Tice did not mention in his 22 June speech that he had been on a trip to Israel last September, funded by a pro-Israel lobbying group.

The trip has been listed in Richard Tice's Declaration of Members' Interests., external

The Parliament code of conduct states the MPs can refer to their entry in the register of interests but adds: "Such a reference will not suffice on its own, as the declaration must provide sufficient information to convey the nature of the interest without the listener or the reader having to have recourse to the Register or other publication."

News.title: Glasgow praised for saving Commonwealth Games as baton passes to Amdavad
News.content:
The man responsible for delivering Glasgow 2026 said the city had "saved and reinvented" the Commonwealth Games, three years after its future was plunged into doubt.

Ahead of Sunday's closing ceremony - which featured a dazzling fireworks display over the River Clyde - Phil Batty recalled how Glasgow stepped up when the original hosts pulled out.

And he believes the legacy of the sustainable, scaled-back Games will shape the future of the multi-sports event.

The Commonwealth flag was last night ceremonially handed over to the Indian city of Amdavad, which will stage the centenary event in 2030.

But Batty said Glasgow's decision to host the event for a second time in 12 years would never be forgotten.

He told BBC Scotland News: "We have created a Games here that will inspire more nations to host but, probably more importantly, that every nation feels it could host at some point in the next 100 years."

News.title: How parents and pupils took on 'cruel', 'authoritarian' schools - and won
News.content:
To avoid getting into trouble, 14-year-old Amelia says she decided to stop drinking water at school so she would not need the toilet.

Her school, Camborne Science and International Academy in Cornwall, had introduced strict disciplinary policies, which included limiting toilet visits during classes, according to pupils and former teachers.

New discipline rules were implemented when the school was taken over in January 2024 by the Athena Learning Trust, which runs six secondary schools in Devon and Cornwall.

Amelia's mother, Kayley, believes these strict policies resulted in her daughter becoming ill from a series of serious infections caused by not drinking.

Hundreds of parents, including Kayley, have campaigned against the way Athena run its schools.

Across Devon and Cornwall, there have been public meetings, school-gate protests and online petitions. Local MPs and councillors have also backed concerned parents.

The opposition to Athena now appears to have paid off - with the trust announcing last month that it was planning to disband and transfer all its schools to other trusts.

It said that trustees had "listened carefully to feedback" and recognised the "clear need for change".

BBC Panorama has spoken to nearly 100 pupils, parents and former teachers from Athena schools, who say levels of discipline went too far. Many pupils and parents queued to talk to us at two town hall meetings we arranged.

The way the schools had been run was "authoritarian" and "cruel", some said.

"You're constantly scared you're going to do something wrong," one student with ADHD told us, while a former music teacher said the strict discipline had meant his lessons were taught in silence.

News.title: Heat health alerts in England as temperatures set to reach 34C
News.content:
Amber and yellow heat health alerts are now in effect across much of England, with temperatures expected to reach 34C in some areas.

The amber alerts, external, issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), cover London, the South East, the East of England and the East Midlands, until 0900 BST on Wednesday 5 August.

The alerts warn that significant impacts are likely across health and social care services due to the high temperatures, including a rise in deaths, particularly among vulnerable people.

Less severe yellow heat heat alerts have also been issued for the same period for the North West, Yorkshire and the Humber, West Midlands and the South West.

The North East is currently the only English region without a heat health alert.

The updated warnings replace those issued during last week's heatwave and reflect a fresh spell of potentially hazardous temperatures expected to affect millions across the country.

News.title: Reform says it would use Navy to stop small boats
News.content:
Reform UK says it would use the Royal Navy to "intercept" small boats crossing the English Channel and return them to France or Belgium.

Under plans to be announced at a news conference, the party says it would form the "largest military operation" in the Channel since World War Two.

When it was put to the party that the UK could not return migrants without French agreement, home affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf claimed it would be possible.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to be "relentless" on tackling small boat crossings, and stressed the UK needs to build a system that offers asylum seekers "safe routes".

More than 2,000 migrants have arrived in the UK on small boats since Burnham became prime minister, and 326 people crossed the English Channel on Saturday. Home Office figures show crossings so far this year are down around 43% compared to the same period in 2025.

Reform's plan called "operation fortress" has been endorsed by "former senior members of our armed forces", Yusuf told BBC Radio 4 Today programme.

It would see Royal Navy vessels intercept all migrant boats in the Channel as part of a humanitarian response.

Yusuf described the scheme as "humanitarian missions" and insisted it would be compatible with rules under the European Convention on Human Rights as Article 2 protects the right to life.

International conventions on the sea allow for states to pick people up from boats if they are in danger of being lost but do not allow for them to be taken to another country without that nation's consent.

Yusuf accepted that the UK and France may have "a diplomatic argument" if French authorities were to refuse to accept migrants escorted back to its shores, but insisted they have a "commitment under international law" to process migrants.

But Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh told BBC Radio 4 Today programme this would mean spending "a lot of time arguing with France".

She agreed the government "absolutely needs to get a grip" on small boat crossings, but said Burnham's team is cracking down on criminal gangs and boosting enforcement.

The prime minister visited Dover at the weekend, where he said the government was "changing the whole approach" to small boats, as the numbers of enforcement officers tackling people-smuggling gangs doubled on both sides of the Channel.

According to the Home Office, the number of National Crime Agency (NCA) officers tackling smuggling gangs facilitating small boat crossings had risen to almost 800 from 376 at the start of 2025.

Reacting to Reform's proposals, retired Royal Navy commander Tom Sharpe told the BBC the UK's border force is better suited to managing migrant arrivals than the navy.

Warships designed for tasks including anti-submarine defences "are not best used for ferrying people around", he explained.

"You're better off using an actual ferry," he said.

Meanwhile, Conservative shadow home secretary Chris Philp insisted that leaving the European Convention on Human Rights should be the government's priority to tackle illegal migration.

"That would enable us to deport every single illegal immigrant within a week of arrival," he told BBC Breakfast. "Either back to their country of origin if possible, or a safe third country, for example Rwanda, if not."

He said this would bring a "deterrent effect" as migrants would no longer cross the channel if they knew they would be deported straight away.

News.title: What are the 'luteal uglies' and how are they affecting women?
News.content:
"Is it just me or am I the ugliest person alive?" a woman in her early 30s asks the camera on TikTok, accompanied by the caption "POV: Girls in their luteal phase."

The video has 2.4 million views and hundreds of comments.

"This is literally me," one woman writes. "I'm angry at how accurate this is," another says.

There are thousands of videos like this one on social media, lamenting the "luteal uglies" - the changes in appearance and mood that women say appear during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle.

During this phase, which occurs in the second half of a woman's cycle and ends when she gets her period, women experience a huge drop in oestrogen. So are the "luteal uglies" a real thing?

According to Dr Louise Newson, a GP and women's hormones specialist, this change in hormone levels means women can experience a shift in their appearance, sleep and mood during this time.

"Our hormones affect our skin, they affect our collagen, so a lot of people find their skin becomes drier, their complexion not so bright, they might have acne and spots," Newson explains. "They might get bloating and breasts can change shape."

News.title: Almost £200,000 of fuel stolen from UK forecourts every day since Iran war began
News.content:
UK drivers have stolen almost Â£200,000 of fuel from petrol stations on average every day since the Iran war broke out and sent prices soaring, according to industry analysis.

Incidents of fuel being taken from forecourts without payment have risen by a fifth in the five months since 28 February, figures from Forecourt Eye suggest.

The conflict in the Middle East severely disrupted oil supplies across the region, triggering a rise in wholesale prices and subsequent increase in costs at the pump in the UK.

Forecourt Eye said the value of the stolen fuel is estimated to have risen by 48% compared with the five months before the war - to reach an estimated daily average of Â£194,000.

The fuel theft prevention company added petrol stations are reporting an increase in "abuse, intimidation and violence from frustrated customers".

The figures are based on a representative sample of 550 forecourts, comparing the five months prior to the outbreak with the five months after it started, and extrapolated to the UK's 8,359 forecourts.

The number of incidents recorded at the forecourts in the sample equates to 2,872 daily incidents on average at forecourts across the UK in the months after war began, up from around 2,400.

They include people driving off without an attempt to pay, and people claiming they have no way to pay after filling their vehicle.

The volume of stolen fuel rose by 24% - up from an estimated 87,000 litres to 108,900 litres a day across all forecourts.

In response, Forecourt Eye said it would partner with facial recognition company Facewatch to offer more than 2,000 retailers free access to crime reporting technology from the autumn.

News.title: I didn't know I'd been hosting a parasite for years - until the most intense pain of my life
News.content:
Jones remembers the May 2016 night when he went into hospital â he was supposed to go out to a dinner with his wife Eileen, but he stayed at home as he felt unwell.

"I hadn't been able to control the pain, and it was more intense than anything I had before.

"Then about midnight, we had to call the ambulance, and they took me to Nevill Hall. Whatever they gave me there cured the pain. I haven't experienced pain like that before."

Jones was in hospital for 10 days, and says the doctors there suspected he had hydatid cysts immediately.

He said: "There was a lot of it around this area at the time, and I remember the Ministry of Agriculture giving worming treatment to the dogs on the local farms.

"Whether they could see that I was an old sheep farmer or not, that might have had a bearing on it. We had plenty of experience in this area â Breconshire as a whole â of hydatid cysts, people that have suffered through it, numerous examples."

Jones was then referred to "the main expert on hydatid cysts" in London where he had two operations in 2018 and 2019 to remove them, one from each lung.

"I swapped two cysts for two scars on the ribs," he said, adding that he still has a cyst on his liver, which surgeons decided not to remove.

News.title: Conservatives call for greater use of facial recognition from police
News.content:
The Conservatives have called for the greater use of facial recognition technology to investigate crimes.

Shadow home secretary Chris Philp wants to make it a requirement for officers to run images of suspects through facial recognition software, where they have been captured on CCTV, mobile phones or camera doorbells.

He also wants officers to follow up when geo-tagged items - including phones, laptops, tablets, bikes and cars - are pinging their location at a suspect's address, as well as tackling stolen goods being sold in plain sight.

A Home Office spokesperson said the government was investing heavily in facial recognition technology.

"This government is already turning the tide on crime," they added.

Philp said the Conservative's Take Back Our Streets plan would put all three elements into practice, backed up by 10,000 extra police officers, which he claimed would be fully funded by Â£800 million per year.

"The public expects clear evidence to always be followed up," he said.

"When they show the police an image of a suspect or the location of stolen goods they want action, not just a crime number."

Labour has pledged an extra 13,000 neighbourhood police by the end of this Parliament. An additional 3,814 officers have been hired between April 2025 and March this year.

Philp praised the existing facial recognition database, which contains images of about 10 million people that can be face-matched using AI, but said what was missing was a requirement on a force to always use it.

Similarly, he said, where a stolen device is pinging its location at an address, an officer will be required to knock on the door.

He added that officers would be required to follow listings of stolen goods advertised online and recover belongings where possible.

"These are the basics the public expect," he said.

News.title: Father felt helpess trying to save son, 7, from sea
News.content:
The father of a seven-year-old boy who died after a beach tragedy said he felt helpless as he tried to battle through waves to save his son.

Musa Ahmed was on a day trip to West Mersea, Essex, on 22 July, when he and five relatives got into difficulty in the water. His teenage cousin and her mother died at the scene.

The seven-year-old was airlifted to the Royal London Hospital, where he died on 28 July.

"Standing before the sea, you quickly realise there are moments when love alone cannot overcome the force of nature," Musa's father, Shahin Ahmed, said in a new statement.

The family had travelled to the island, near Colchester, from Barking in east London that morning.

Three others were also taken to hospital by ambulance after the incident, first reported to Essex Police at 17:35 BST, and were said by the force to be "recovering".

Ahmed, has previously said the group were swept away by a "very strong" tide and police said they made "significant efforts to help each other".

He has said he now wants to honour his son's memory by creating a programme to provide young people with first aid and water safety training in a bid to save others.

News.title: Burnham pledges to be 'relentless' in curbing small boat crossings
News.content:
Andy Burnham has pledged his government will be "relentless" in curbing the number of people arriving in the UK on small boats.

The prime minister said progress had been made and the government was "changing the whole approach", with enforcement officers tackling people-smuggling gangs doubled on both sides of the Channel.

"People want to see this issue addressed," he said in Dover, adding: "We also need to build a system that offers safe routes for people as well, because that also takes away the selling point of the gangs."

The Conservatives said that Labour had not delivered on its promises on migration, while Reform UK said if in government it would deploy the navy to ward off crossings.

Political discussions around the UK's policies on illegal migration have resurfaced since tens of thousands of migrants swam into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on Thursday.

Burnham noted that 98% of the people who swam to the African territory had been returned to Morocco - which he said had dealt with the immediate issue.

But he added: "There's a broader issue about the Schengen area and our relationship with it, and of course, I would want to be in regular dialogue with the EU on those issues."

His comments came shortly after the Home Office announced that the number of National Crime Agency (NCA) officers tackling smuggling gangs facilitating small boat crossings had risen to almost 800 from 376 at the start of 2025.

Burnham said there had been a similar doubling of French officers.

Asked whether he wanted to change the tone of the debate around small boats, he said that he wanted to "deal with the issue rather than play politics with the issue".

He added: "The public don't like the idea that the border looks like it's not controlled. We need to bring back that control. But also we need to offer support for people who genuinely need it."

News.title: Man arrested after death of nine-year-old girl found injured in industrial estate
News.content:
A man has been arrested after the death of a nine-year-old girl who was found with serious injuries in Arbroath.

Officers were called to the town's Elliot Industrial Estate shortly after midnight.

The girl was taken to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she later died.

A 35-year-old man has been arrested in connection with her death, which is being treated as suspicious.

A police forensics tent has been erected at the scene and a cordon has been put in place.

Police Scotland said the girl's family were being supported by specialist officers and inquiries were continuing.

News.title: At least five Al Fayed survivors confirmed as modern slavery victims
News.content:
At least five women who were abused by former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed have been formally recognised by the Home Office as victims of modern slavery.

The BBC revealed in April that Rachel Louw, who has waived her right to anonymity, had become the first woman known to receive such a decision.

Since then, at least four other women have received positive "conclusive grounds" decisions recognising them as victims of modern slavery, with more expected to follow, according to PA Media.

The latest cases include women who were trafficked internationally and within the UK, including one case in which the trafficking took place entirely within Harrods.

When an individual receives a positive "conclusive grounds" decision through the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) - the UK's official framework for identifying victims of modern slavery - they are formally recognised as a victim.

Legal experts have previously told the BBC that these decisions can strengthen the credibility of witnesses in criminal proceedings and may influence the way police investigate cases.

The Modern Slavery Act, which came into force in 2015, defines human trafficking as arranging or facilitating the travel of another person within a country or across borders for the purposes of that person being exploited.

The latest decisions include all four members of the survivor advocacy group No One Above, who had been awaiting rulings after being referred to the NRM by the anti-slavery charity Unseen.

According to PA Media, one survivor had been recruited to a false role within Harrods, while two others were employed in legitimate roles before being selected for abuse from the shop floor.

A fourth worked as a domestic employee for the Fayed family after being recruited by a letting agency called Hyde Park Residence.

One of the survivors said receiving the decision was "very significant".

"Seeing it in writing that you were a victim of modern slavery and trafficking is very... it's really shocking to read," she told PA Media.

News.title: Man admits transporting Scottish woman's body in suitcase, Greek police say
News.content:
Greek police say a man has admitted transporting the body of a Scottish woman in a suitcase to an abandoned building.

Elisabeth-Jane Ross, 38, was found in the Kypseli district of Athens on 18 July, days after she was reported missing.

Local officers launched an investigation with cooperation from authorities in the US, the UK and Scotland, and now say they have arrested a 26-year-old man - the BBC understands he is from Afghanistan.

The force said he was brought to police headquarters on Thursday where he "confessed to his actions". He was arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, robbery and weapons offences, but the exact charges have yet to be finalised under the Greek legal system.

News.title: Man seen pulling weapons out of car before Idaho In-n-Out shooting
News.content:
A man was seen pulling out weapons from a car before a shooting that began at an In-N-Out Burger in Idaho on Saturday afternoon (1 August).

Three people were killed, and at least seven people were injured in the incident, Twin Falls Police Chief Matthew Hicks told a press conference.

The shooter died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said on Sunday.

An off-duty state trooper and a member of the public actively engaged the suspect by returning gunfire, police said.

Authorities believe that the 24-year-old suspect, identified as Chad Williams, acted alone. The suspect’s movements and motivations leading up to the shooting in a shopping area are yet to be determined, Hicks added.

A grieving family mistakenly told they would inherit £30,000 in Premium Bonds by National Savings and Investments (NS&I) were awarded compensation.

The family had planned to use the money to fund funeral costs before the error was revealed, one member told the Financial Ombudsman.

Identified as ‘Mr B’, he said NS&I had written to him following the passing of his relative, Ms B, to inform him she held Premium Bonds worth around £30,000 at the time of her death.

The Treasury-backed bank later wrote again to Mr B to inform him it had mistaken the deceased with another Premium Bonds customer who has a similar name.

Ms B had no active accounts with NS&I at the time of her death, and had withdrawn her funds several years prior, it added.

The complainant had sought £15,000 in compensation from the Treasury-backed bank, but was finally awarded only £300 – two per cent of this figure.

A grieving family was mistakenly told they would inherit £30,000 in Premium Bonds ( Getty )

This covered the cost of the grant of probate NS&I had requested from Mr B in its initial letter to process the estate’s funds.

Mr B had argued NS&I should also cover funeral costs of £5,335 due to the error. He had previously agreed with other family members to pool funds for some arrangements, he told the ombudsman, but after receiving the letter told them the expected money could be used instead.

However, ombudsman Katy Kidd found the investment company was not liable for these costs, concluding they had not arisen as a direct result of the mistaken letter.

Regarding the funeral costs, Ms Kidd wrote: “I can understand the difficulty of Mr B’s position here. But I’m afraid I don’t think NS&I needs to meet these costs.”

She also states NS&I had previously recognised that Mr B “personally suffered distress and inconvenience due to its mistake”, for which it sent a letter apologising for “the upset caused [and] the immense error it had made”.

The investment company is understood to have already paid £175 in compensation before the ruling.

An NS&I spokesperson said: “We sincerely apologise that on this occasion we have not provided the customer service that people should expect from NS&I, particularly at such a sensitive time.”

The ruling comes after it was revealed in March that administrative failures by NS&I had caused £367 million to not be paid into the accounts of 37,500 bereaved families.

Former chief executive Dax Harkins resigned over the episode in March, with work to compensate the affected families understood to be underway.

News.title: Record low Danube levels push some countries in Eastern Europe to the brink of energy emergency
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Numerous governments across Central and Eastern Europe are taking steps to conserve electricity and avert an energy crisis as record low water levels on the Danube River have forced power plants to the brink of shutting down.

Persistent drought and successive extreme heat waves have deprived one of Europe's largest rivers of water, pushing the Danube's levels in Hungary's capital Budapest to around 10 centimeters (4 inches) on Monday, well below the previous all-time low of 33 centimeters (13 inches) set in 2018.

Water levels are not expected to rise on the Danube in the coming days or even weeks as no significant rainfall is forecast, and as a renewed extreme heat wave bears down on the region with daytime highs topping 38 Celsius (100 Fahrenheit), electricity and water use are on the rise.

Hungary's Paks nuclear plant on brink of shutdown

The Danube's record low levels have pushed Hungary's only nuclear power plant, the Soviet-built, four-reactor plant at Paks, to the brink of powering down entirely for the first time in its 44 years in service.

The Paks plant, which uses water from the Danube to cool its reactors, on Monday was producing only 240 megawatts of power rather than the usual 2,000 due to successive power-downs of its four reactors.

In video posted to Facebook on Monday, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said engineers had managed to keep the plan’s final operating turbine temporarily running, averting an expected shutdown on the weekend. A full power-down will likely only happen on Tuesday or Wednesday, Magyar said.

“This is very good news, because the complete shutdown of the Paks power plant can still be avoided, at least temporarily, on one of the biggest consumption days,” he said.

The Paks plant, located around 90 kilometers (55 miles) south of Budapest, accounts for nearly half of Hungary’s electricity production and around a third of its consumption. Hungary has relied on regional electricity imports as well as renewable sources to try to make up for the deficit from the Paks plant.

Hungary’s government last week asked major industrial users to curb their electricity consumption and sought voluntary savings from households in order to conserve supply, particularly in peak demand hours between 5 p.m. and 10 p.m.

It also announced that electric-powered freight trains would not be permitted to run during peak hours beginning on Monday in order to conserve an estimated 70 to 90 megawatt-hours of electricity per day.

While conservation measures were initially voluntary, Magyar’s government on Saturday issued a decree allowing for them to be made mandatory for large industrial or commercial consumers.

He said Monday that the conservation push had resulted in 700 fewer megawatts of electricity being used the previous day, and thanked Hungarians for their efforts.

Serbia and Romania grapple with low Danube levels

Meanwhile, plants in neighboring countries have also seen dramatic drops in power generation, as well as disruptions to shipping and agriculture.

Serbia’s record-low Danube levels have pushed the country’s key hydroelectric plant to operate with only 20% of its capacity, prompting Prime Minister Djuro Macut to preside over an emergency meeting on Monday focusing on energy problems.

Macut appealed to residents to “minimize the use of big consumers of electricity in their homes, such as air conditioners.” He described the situation in a statement late on Sunday as “serious and demanding.”

Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has predicted that the Danube could become too low for river transport in just a few days, and while cargo ships are still able to run for the time being, they must carry 50% less weight than usual.

In Romania, where Danube water flow has fallen to 1,500 cubic meters per second, less than a third of its July average, authorities have shut down a reactor unit at the Cernavoda power plant for safety reasons, and further power downs are planned. The plant is operating at about half its normal capacity.

___

Associated Press writer Jovana Gec in Belgrade, Serbia, contributed to this report.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday morning to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Speaking on board Air Force One on Sunday, Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr Trump said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes.

The US president said on Saturday that he had halted plans for a massive attack against Iran, which he said would have been the biggest since World War Two, saying the “perimeter” of a deal was there.

The sharp fall in the oil price that followed also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The latest around Iran is that hopes have risen over the weekend of a diplomatic off-ramp.”

Oil prices are down markedly from their peak of more than $126 a barrel in April, when prices had surged by 74pc in two months.

However, they remain 14pc higher since the US and Israel began their war with Iran on February 28 and climbed as high as $100 in July amid fresh clashes in the Gulf. Monday’s fall means oil is at its lowest since July 13.

Petrol prices hit their highest level since the start of the conflict on Friday, with unleaded up to 160p per litre, according to the RAC.

Petrol is now the most expensive it has been since 2022, when Russia’s invasion of Ukraine sent energy prices surging.

If sustained, the fall in oil prices will provide relief for John Healey, the new Chancellor, who pledged in The Telegraph at the weekend that he would watch out for “any suggestions that customers are being taken for a ride at the pump or the till”.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

News.title: Josh Kerr turns ‘race of the century’ into one-sided show of power
News.content:
“It means everything – absolutely incredible,” said Kerr, who joined the rendition of Flower of Scotland before closing his eyes to soak up the moment in a stadium where he had competed as a child in even the shot put.

“To do it in front of a Scottish crowd, where I learned how to race, doesn’t get any better,” he added. “I came here week after week growing up as a kid. This was the championship of my season with the world indoors and going after the record. This was on the calendar before any of that. I think a British crowd deserved more from me and I owed them that.”

Of the tactics compared to his world record, where he had to hold an even pace throughout, Kerr stressed the importance of staying calm and not being tempted into pushing too soon. “London was a big stress, pushing my body to the extreme limit,” he said. “Doing a championship race is a nice clean slate; using your brain instead of your body. It’s how I love to race.

“When you’re running that slow, your job is not to waste energy and I did that. I knew an opportunity would open up. Then it was about staying awake and alive and trying to get some space. felt like I had plenty of gears left in me.”

Kerr had emerged to a huge home ovation and, with the Proclaimers booming out as the runners completed the first two laps, he was content to stay in the pack even as Myers followed. There was then only one brief moment of concern as the runners began gathering themselves during the penultimate lap and Kerr became momentarily boxed in.

News.title: Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid
News.content:
Manchester United 2 Atletico Madrid 1

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

News.title: City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter
News.content:
Manchester City 1 Inter Milan 1; Inter win 3-1 on pens

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

News.title: Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur 2 Chelsea 1

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.



Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal medical, Liverpool signing jets in, Man Utd prepare £60m bid
Sports.content:
The latest Manchester United, Liverpool, Arsenal transfer news and more as the likes of Bruno Guimaraes, Vinicius Jr and Bradley Barcola's futures remain up in the air

Welcome to Mirror Football's transfer news live blog on Monday, August 3.

The transfer window is entering the business end of the summer with less than three weeks to go until the Premier League kicks into action. Arsenal are primed to make a splash as they attempt to get some major deals over the line to launch their title defence.

The Gunners are reportedly nearing a move for Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes and are primed to move for Vinicius Junior should the Brazilian winger be unable to agree a new contract with Real Madrid. An approach for Julian Alvarez hasn't been ruled out either.

Manchester United, meanwhile are looking to add a third midfielder following the signings of Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. However, they are being increasingly linked to Magpies full-back Lewis Hall following Eddie Howe's departure.

Elsewhere, Liverpool are said to be interested in a big-money move for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola, while Tottenham's heavy spending could continue with a move for Victor Osimhen.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino was set to earn huge salary from World Cup plan as staggering figure revealed

FIFA boss Gianni Infantino was set to pocket an eye-watering amount should his controversial World Cup idea succeeded

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has U-turned on the plan to sell a share in the World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA chief Gianni Infantino was reportedly set to pocket a staggering £47 million per year had his plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup succeeded. Infantino, 56, came under heavy fire after the failed unveiling of his plans to sell off fractions in FIFA competitions to private investors.

‌



The FIFA president's idea plunged the football world into chaos. However, he pulled off a dramatic U-turn after considerable backlash, with pressure now mounting on the Swiss and support for his re-election collapsing.

‌



Infantino's plan was to create a private, investment-open company to run its flagship competitions and raise billions of pounds. It was believed to be led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of Jared Kushner, the US President Donald Trump's son-in-law.

‌



The FIFA chief, 56, had orchestrated a plan to sell 20 per cent stake in the new sister company to private investors for a reported £3.1m.

UEFA threatened a wide-ranging boycott of any FIFA tournaments, while fellow federations such as CONCACAF and AFC also publicised their opposition to the plan.

English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot READ MORE :

FIFA boss Infantino under pressure as UK FA member pulls support READ MORE :

Infantino currently earns a salary of around £2.6m as FIFA president, although his total figure is said to have doubled last year following bonuses. A new role as commissioner of the FIFA Forward Enterprise would, according to The Times, have landed him a salary similar to that of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell, who takes home around £47m per year.

‌



Infantino has been president of FIFA since February 2016, having replaced Sepp Blatter. However, in the wake of his plan falling flat, he is facing unprecedented criticism.

A FIFA statement released last week claimed the idea has been scrapped. Nevertheless, UEFA has declared a loss of confidence in Infantino after the scandal, with the Welsh and English FAs becoming the first nations to publicly withdraw their support for the FIFA boss to be re-elected.

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino has been criticised this summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



UEFA's statement read: "We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

"It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again. That review should be thorough and fundamental.

"No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

‌



View 3 Images UEFA has 'lost confidence' in Gianni Infantino (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's Member Associations to elect him as their President in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent. I have been this in the last 15 years of my life in UEFA. You will have to play a part every day in the life of FIFA,' before telling the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA President. It's your money. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else.'

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through were anything but transparent."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sends Vinicius Jr transfer message ahead of Real Madrid meeting

Mikel Arteta is now leading Arsenal's transfer pursuit of Vinicius Junior, with the Real Madrid star returning to training with his future at the Bernabeu unresolved

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is leading Arsenal's push (Image: Alex Caparros, Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is spearheading Arsenal's move to sign Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid this summer. The Gunners are in hot pursuit of the Brazil star, and he has been informed that he would play a central role at the Emirates.

‌



Arsenal have been strongly linked with a move for the Real Madrid star amid uncertainty over whether he will agree to fresh terms with Los Blancos. Vinicius has just 12 months left on his deal at the Bernabeu, and the north London side are looking to take advantage of the uncertainty.

‌



Despite his contract situation, it is reported that a transfer fee could still climb as high as £130million to secure the forward's services. Arteta and co have stressed to the player that Arsenal's project would be built largely around him, a proposition that carries less weight in the Spanish capital, according to AS.

‌



Arsenal's chase comes as Vinicius holds talks with Real Madrid following his return from the summer break. The two-time Champions League winner's verdict is expected to arrive after his discussions with the La Liga club's hierarchy.

Real Madrid are said to be unwilling to revise their latest contract proposal to Vinicius and believe the ball is now firmly in the player's court. The Gunners are prepared to make a significant contract offer.

Arsenal handed Bruno Guimaraes boost as Newcastle change their transfer stance READ MORE :

Should he opt against extending his stay, Real Madrid will entertain offers for his departure. It has been previously reported that Vinicius is in no hurry to commit his future, though new manager Jose Mourinho was prepared to intervene to retain his prized assets.

‌



Arsenal have been transparent about their aspirations this summer, despite refusing to be drawn specifically on the Real Madrid star. Arteta has acknowledged that the Gunners have scope to develop.

"A lot is happening. We all know about the context of this transfer window," the Gunners boss said.

View 2 Images Vinicus Junior has returned to Real Madrid training (Image: Justin Setterfield, Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level. That is going to require a better squad, better individuals.

"We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully, very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

‌



Arsenal are also pursuing Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. Vinicius' compatriot is reportedly keen on a switch to the Emirates as the Magpies contend with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe.

It has been suggested that a medical is arranged for Guimaraes, though reports from the north east have indicated that speculation of a transfer being finalised are hasty.

Sports.title: English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot
Sports.content:
English FA follow Wales in withdrawing Gianni Infantino support after botched World Cup plot

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has lost support from nations within the game after unveiling a controversial - and now abandoned - plan to sell off World Cup stakes

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's position is in jeopardy (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The Football Association will withdraw their support for Gianni Infantino to be re-elected as FIFA president following his recent attempt to sell off stakes in the World Cup.

‌



Infantino has been under heavy fire in recent days following the unsuccessful unveiling of his plans to sell off stakes in FIFA competitions to private investors, which was abandoned following a ferocious backlash.

‌



The fallout from the ordeal is likely to have a detrimental impact on Infantino's bid to remain in his post as FIFA president for another term.

‌



And it has now been claimed by The Times that the English FA will withdraw a previous letter of support backing Infantino to remain as president.

FIFA boss Infantino under pressure as UK FA member pulls support READ MORE :

They follow the Welsh FA in doing so with more likely to follow suit with football's other governing bodies now expected to try and oust Infantino from his post. Wales were the first nation to pull their support for Infantino, who was seeking re-election next year.

Both England and Wales were among the nations who were willing to boycott future World Cups had Infantino's scheme not been pulled, as confirmed in a statement by UEFA.

‌



The European governing body has been particularly scathing of Infantino since he unveiled his plans and stressed that confidence in the 56-year-old has now evaporated.

"The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family," UEFA's statement read.

View 2 Images Infantino has been haemorrhaging support since his botched World Cup sale plans were unveiled (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"When Gianni Infantino asked for the trust and the votes of FIFA's member associations to elect him as their president in 2016, he said, 'Of course we have to be transparent'.

"He told the assembled stakeholders, 'The money of FIFA is your money. It's not the money of the FIFA president. You are the national associations and the money of FIFA has to serve for the development of football and not for anything else'.

"On both these promises, he has failed to deliver. The shabby, back room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent."

Sports.title: 4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality
Sports.content:
4 transfers Liverpool need to complete after Leeds defeat showed harsh reality

Liverpool were beaten 4-2 by Premier League rivals Leeds in the final game of their US tour, underlining the work that needs to be done in the transfer market to add to Andoni Iraola's squad

Liverpool players react to pre-season defeat to Leeds in Chicago

The proper stuff is now less than three weeks away and Liverpool still have work to do in the transfer market.

‌



Andoni Iraola has been getting to know the squad he inherited on the club's pre-season tour of the United States, concluding with a 4-2 defeat to Leeds on Sunday. Goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz had the Reds 2-0 up at half-time but Leeds ran riot in the second half, scoring four goals in 25 minutes to win the game.

‌



Liverpool's new manager has yet to work with some key figures following the World Cup, with Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister both absent for the tour.

‌



However, Iraola will want Liverpool to be active in the transfer window before they travel to Newcastle for their Premier League curtain-raiser on August 23. Here are four signings Liverpool could make before the transfer deadline.

Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points READ MORE :

View 4 Images Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola is in need of some new recruits (Image: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock)

1. A centre-back

Liverpool have been rocked by bad luck in the central defensive areas. Giovanni Leoni signed last year before sustaining an ACL injury on his debut, while Jeremy Jacquet, another new buy, has yet to feature in pre-season and missed out here.

‌



With Van Dijk also absent, a very youthful backline wilted under a barrage of Leeds pressure in the second half. And while Van Dijk would have made a huge difference, it still feels as though Liverpool need at least one more centre-back - especially with Joe Gomez also set to miss the start of the season.

2. A left-back

View 4 Images Andy Robertson left Liverpool at the end of last season (Image: Jack Thomas, Getty Images)

Milos Kerkez was part of last summer's spending splurge that failed to yield consecutive Premier League titles for Liverpool. But the Hungary international did find his feet after a challenging start to the season and finished the campaign looking like the player who flourished at Bournemouth to earn a big-money move.

‌



Kerkez will undoubtedly start the season as first-choice, but quality depth and competition in that area is a must following Andy Robertson's exit. Kostas Tsimikas spent last season out on loan and could provide that. Or the Greece international could be moved on for good.

And while Chambers, impressive at centre-back in the win over Wrexham and on the scoresheet here, has impressed Iraola in pre-season, it would probably be a big ask for the rookie full-back to be Kerkez's deputy.

3. A right winger

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola has emerged as Liverpool's big summer target (Image: Anne-Christine POUJOULAT / AFP via Getty Images)

‌



While the Leeds game highlighted the deficiencies in Liverpool's makeshift defence, they are still operating with a Mohamed Salah-sized hope in attack.

Finding the right successor to Liverpool's Egyptian King is an absolute must if they are to enjoy a better season this time around. Bradley Barcola has seemingly emerged as their preferred target, although any deal is unlikely to be cheap and could result in Liverpool spending in excess of £100million on a player for the THIRD time in 12 months.

Whether it's Barcola or somebody else, adding a right winger is a non-negotiatiable for Liverpool. And given whoever does come in will be following Anfield royalty in the role, they could do with ample time bedding in. So getting a deal down is a priority.

‌



4. A central midfielder

View 4 Images Curtis Jones could move on this summer (Image: 2026 Liverpool FC)

With Curtis Jones looking likely to move on this summer, Liverpool could do with another central midfielder to make sure Iraola isn't left short.

Intriguingly, could the answer come from within? Harvey Elliott's time at Anfield looked up to be up when he joined Aston Villa on a loan move with an obligation last summer, only to be frozen out. Or how about the impressive Trey Nyoni, who has a big impression in pre-season.

Article continues below

Maybe it's too early for Nyoni. And maybe Elliott will join Jones in moving on permanently this summer. Either way, a new face in midfield would be welcomed.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola to add three players to squad as £80m transfer given backing
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola to add three players to squad as £80m transfer given backing

Liverpool's transfer business is expected to pick up speed as the clock ticks down on this summer's window

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola is set to oversee his first campaign with Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

The countdown is on with Liverpool facing Newcastle in their opening game of the Premier League season on August 23. It's slowly becoming critical that the Reds act in the transfer window, sooner rather than later, with surgery on their squad still required.

‌



Victor Munoz is the club's only arrival after signing for £34.5 million from Spanish side Osasuna. Losing Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate means Liverpool are in need not only of more personnel but also of experience.

‌



Today's latest sees Iraola give fans a boost with a squad announcement. Elsewhere, the Reds have been backed to launch a spectacular bid for a Premier League star.

‌



Iraola makes three player announcement

Reds' head coach Iraola has confirmed that Victor Munoz, Alisson Becker and Alexis Mac Allister will join up with his squad in the coming weeks.

All three have been given extended time off due to their participation in the World Cup, with Munoz and Mac Allister both reaching the final of the tournament with Spain and Argentina, respectively. Munoz and Alisson are set to report to training this week once the Reds arrive back in England after their pre-season tour of the USA.

On Munoz, Iraola told the club's official website on Saturday: "Yes, he comes next week. We spoke to him and he wanted also to come a little bit earlier than the three weeks that they have the right to have, because obviously he is coming to a new club, he will need some time to adapt, to meet his teammates. We will have him next week as soon as we arrive there, basically. It’s good news."

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Yan Diomande transfer twist as surprise update emerges on Real Madrid target READ MORE :

Liverpool have been given green light for 'dream' Bradley Barcola alternative READ MORE :

Iraola added: "Yes, Alisson will be there from the first day. He was arriving to AXA a little bit later than Cody [Gakpo] and Virgil [van Dijk]. But he will be [there] since the first day that we arrive and will start training there in Liverpool.

View 3 Images Victor Munoz recently signed for Liverpool (Image: Johnnie Izquierdo - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



Addressing Mac Allister's return, the Basque head coach said the midfielder will return around August 9, the date Liverpool play Monaco in a pre-season fixture.

He said: "Alexis will have, I think, until the Monaco game. I think deserved holidays for him; long season, long World Cup, played until the final, has played a lot of minutes. I hope he comes fully recovered and he enjoys also the break that he definitely has earned."

Club icon backs move for £80m star

Former Liverpool star Vladimir Smicer has instructed Liverpool to move for Bournemouth's £80m-rated midfielder Alex Scott. The 22-year-old has been linked with a move to Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea, who have already had a bid of around £65m turned down for the player.

‌



Smicer, who won the Champions League with the Reds in 2005, believes Iraola's relationship with Scott, with the Basque previously coaching Scott on the South Coast, could sweeten a deal should Liverpool move for the player.

"I think you can expect Andoni Iraola would like to take Alex Scott because he knows what he can do," Smicer said, via Casinostugan.

"To be honest, in midfield we need a bit more spark with people who are fighting but are clever going forward, turning quickly with the ball and finding strikers. Of course, we expect a lot from (Florian) Wirtz to do this. But Andoni Iraola knows Alex Scott. If the price is right and he sees the possibility to strengthen the team, why not?

‌



View 3 Images Alex Scott starred for Bournemouth last season (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

"Curtis Jones is linked with a few moves, and if he leaves, we need midfield press. We don't know what's happening with (Alexis) Mac Allister, he had a bit of a weak season and was not at the same level. (Ryan) Gravenberch had a good start, but then it was not the best. Only (Dominik) Szoboszlai was a top player in midfield for the whole season.

"In midfield you need competition, and Scott can be a great asset because he's only twenty-two and is playing regularly for the England youth teams. He's a good prospect and a local guy from the UK.

Article continues below

"These things are important. I don't know if he would love to play for Liverpool, but not many players would turn them down. He's got a good chance now because Andoni Iraola is the new manager. If he likes him, I think we can find the money."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly transfer boost as medical booked and star 'says yes' to move
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Myles Lewis-Skelly transfer boost as medical booked and star 'says yes' to move

Manchester United are enjoying an under-the-radar transfer window as they continue to target a handful of positions

View 3 Images Michael Carrick is enjoying his first pre-season as Manchester United manager (Image: Getty)

Manchester United are one game closer to the new Premier League season. And Michael Carrick's squad has so far only been bolstered by three new senior arrivals.

‌



United fans were made to wait for their club to spring into action this window but were rewarded by a flurry of incomings. Andrey Santos was quickly followed by ex-Leeds United goalkeeper Karl Darlow and Youri Tielemans through the door. Young prospects in Tynan Thompson and Kit Margetson were also snapped up.

‌



Their latest pre-season outing saw them defeat Atletico Madrid 2-1 in Stockholm. But one position that the club are keen to reinforce is left-back. Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui can operate there, but a surprise move for Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly has been mooted.

‌



United have long held an interest in the defender and another transfer that might be completed this week could enable Carrick's side to pounce. Mirror Football takes a look at the latest transfer news out of Old Trafford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

Marcus Rashford has chance to 'hurt' Man Utd as two transfer moves proposed READ MORE :

Myles Lewis-Skelly boost

United were first linked with Lewis-Skelly last year when he found himself falling down the left-back pecking order at Arsenal. Both Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie were getting more minutes.

‌



View 3 Images Lewis-Skelly was a Premier League title winner last season (Image: Getty)

This was soon resolved when Mikel Arteta moved the 19-year-old into midfield and he impressed. However, Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes is set for a Gunners medical on Monday, according to The Times. If the Brazilian does sign, he'll become one more star Lewis-Skelly has to compete with for first-team minutes. Not to mention, his reported £80m transfer sum will leave a dent.

Any fee Arsenal get from selling Lewis-Skelly would be pure profit when taking into account Financial Fair Play (FFP) regulations, so if United lodge the right offer, it could be too good to turn down.

‌



The Independent reports that they are currently waiting to see whether the Gunners are open to doing business regarding Lewis-Skelly and that United's interest remains strong.

Man Utd star 'agrees' to move

On the outgoings front, reports from Italy suggest Joshua Zirkzee has agreed to join Juventus on loan with no obligation to buy. The Dutch forward does not appear to be part of Carrick's first-team plans.

View 3 Images Zirkzee has reportedly agreed to join Juventus (Image: Getty)

‌



United bought Zirkzee for £36m in 2024 and he became the first signing under the ownership of INEOS. He previously played in Italy with Bologna.

It is understood that Zirkzee has become a difficult player to sell and, having not been able to cut it at United, is far more likely to head out on loan, either with or without an option to buy.

La Gazzetta dello Sport claims that Zirkzee has agreed to such a deal with Juventus and has already 'said yes' to the Italian outfit. However, the move is hinging on the Old Lady being able to offload striker Jonathan David.
