The Leeds comeback commenced with a mistake by Kerkez. His over-elaborate back-heel was seized on by Ethan Ampadu, who released Aaronson in space on the left of the Liverpool penalty area. The USA international beat Giorgi Mamardashvili with a confident low finish. Calvert-Lewin levelled from close range after Joe Rodon flicked on a long throw from Ampadu and, just two minutes later, a third of Farke’s half-time substitutes put Leeds ahead in slapstick fashion. Jones attempted to sweep away Aaronson’s low cross into the Liverpool area and succeeded only in turning the ball against Longstaff. The Leeds midfielder looked sheepish after the rebound trickled beyond a stunned Mamardashvili.

Leeds were not done there. Worryingly for Iraola, his team were undone by an identical routine to Calvert-Lewin’s first goal. Another Ampadu long throw, another flick on, this time by the commanding new recruit Tarik Muharemovic, and the former Everton striker inflicted more punishment on Liverpool by converting a towering header off the underside of the crossbar.

Sports.title: Chelsea sign Argentina international Valentín Barco from Strasbourg
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed the Argentina international Valentín Barco from their sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year deal.

The 22-year-old, who played seven times for Brighton including six Premier League appearances during the 2023-24 season, becomes the eighth arrival of new manager Xabi Alonso’s reign.

A versatile player who can be used in central midfield as well as his regular position of left-back, Barco was in the Argentina squad that finished as runners-up at the World Cup, winning his fifth cap in the 3-1 group-stage win over Jordan.

He moved to Strasbourg initially on loan from Brighton in 2025 and signed permanently later that year having helped the club to qualify for the Conference League. In all he made 54 appearances for the Ligue 1 side.

He was involved in a heated exchange with England’s Jude Bellingham immediately after his side’s 2-1 World Cup semi-final win in Atlanta, with Bellingham appearing to clip Barco around the head. The Argentinian, who was an unused substitute, had earlier run on to the pitch to celebrate after Enzo Fernández had equalised. He is expected to join up shortly with his new teammates on their tour of Australia and Hong Kong.

It continues a busy summer in the transfer market for Chelsea as they look to remodel under Alonso. On Saturday they confirmed the signing of the veteran striker Danny Welbeck from Brighton, following the signings of Crystal Palace’s Maxence Lacroix and Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. Denner, Marco Palestra, Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda have also been signed.

Sports.title: Socceroos on the move: Herrington headlines post-World Cup transfers
Sports.content:
Lucas Herrington, fresh off becoming the youngest Australian to start a game at a men’s World Cup, is set to become the second-most expensive footballer in Australian history with a move to newly-promoted Premier League side Hull City. Latest reports suggest a fee of approximately £12.6m ($24.1m), with a further £4.4m ($8.4m) in add-ons, which comes in just shy of the Australian record of £15m plus £5m in add-ons ($38.3m in total) that Leicester paid Stoke City to sign Harry Souttar in 2023.

It would set a new selling high-water mark for his current club, Colorado Rapids, and eclipses the decade-old record Hull set when they paid just over £10m for Ryan Mason. Given the trajectory of Herrington’s meteoric rise, it feels a pretty safe bet to assume the 18-year-old will claim Souttar’s record outright sooner rather than later.

Hull may not be quite as attractive as a move to Barcelona or Liverpool, both of whom were linked to Herrington in recent months. But such a view overlooks that it was only a few years ago that a lack of representation in major European leagues was decried. Clubs in those competitions are now paying record fees for Australia’s brightest young talents.

The only cohort in Australia that should be perturbed by the deal is those connected to Brisbane Roar, having watched as the club (which as a reminder, is granted a monopoly over Queensland by the A-League Men’s current closed nature) sold their sell-on fee back to the Rapids for a reported $560,000. It meant the club missed out on a minimum $4.8m, not even a year on from Herrington’s departure.

Importantly, in moving to Hull’s MKM Stadium rather than the Camp Nou or Anfield for such a significant fee, the central defender should ostensibly be able to play the regular senior football that will maintain his remarkable rise. Even if Hull prove to be one-and-done in the English top-flight, Herrington will still be a teenager at the end of this season, battle-hardened by a year of playing on club football’s biggest stage on his resume.

Barring disaster, it should only help establish his future at that level, as well as help develop his game in a manner in which the Socceroos can reap the benefits.

Herrington is not the only member of the young cohort from Tony Popovic’s Socceroos squad that looks set to capitalise on appearing at the World Cup, even if the days of the tournament serving as a one-stop shop for the transfer market have long since passed. In the days of modern analytics and digitised global scouting, no player is ever truly off the radar.

Herrington is one of eight players aged 23 or under who started a game in North America. Since the tournament ended, Paul-Okon Engstler sealed a move from Sydney FC to Bundesliga outfit FC Köln, while breakout goalkeeper Patrick Beach concluded a move seven months in the making when he shifted in the City Football Group from Melbourne City to newly-promoted Ligue 1 side Troyes.

View image in fullscreen Paul Okon-Engstler appears in a pre-season friendly for his new club FC Köln. Photograph: Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

The moves of Okon-Engstler and Beach are notable in that they are making the jump straight from the A-League Men to one of Europe’s big five leagues, with early indications from pre-season suggesting they’re chances to start or see decent minutes. Is it remarkable, given the last time Australian players successfully went directly from the Australian top-flight to regular minutes in one of these leagues was in the days of Vince Grella and Stan Lazaridis – who left NSL sides Carlton and West Adelaide, respectively.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There is still plenty of development ahead for the likes of Herrington, Beach and Okon-Engstler. Simply getting to these leagues isn’t the end of the journey, but the start of a new one. But add to this Champions League-bound Sporting CP’s reported pursuit of Nestory Irankunda (on a deal that should eclipse Souttar’s if it goes through) and the Premier League clubs that were circling Jordy Bos before his unfortunate injury against Egypt forced him to undergo surgery, and it substantiates the excitement around the young talent coming through Australian football’s pathways.

And though not of the same age cohort, a strong World Cup also has Souttar, still the Socceroos rock, on the verge of a Championship move, with Sheffield United and Wrexham his reported suitors in a move that should give him much-needed stability and hopes of a promotion push.

Mathew Ryan, after playing a major role in staving off relegation last season, has inked a return to La Liga side Levante for the 2026-27 campaign. In a significant boost to his chances of staying in the Socceroos mix, Tete Yengi has secured a permanent move to J-League side Machida Zelvia after spending the end of last season on loan, while Cammy Devlin has followed Derek McInnes from Hearts to Rangers. Ajdin Hrustić, meanwhile, has moved to UAE outfit Al-Nasr.

Sports.title: Three Premier League clubs, including a newly-promoted side, enquire over Mykhailo Mudryk after £89m Chelsea winger's doping case is resolved
Sports.content:
Three Premier League clubs, including a newly-promoted side, enquire over Mykhailo Mudryk after £89m Chelsea winger's doping case is resolved

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have received multiple approaches about Mykhailo Mudryk from clubs following the news of his return to football – including three from the Premier League.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport.

All options are open between Mudryk and Chelsea this summer, including whether to send him out on loan after his sudden comeback from a doping suspension.

The current plan is for the 25-year-old Ukrainian to be assessed by Xabi Alonso, having travelled to Hong Kong to join his team-mates on their pre-season tour.

Chelsea want to see where their player’s performance levels are now at, with the Ukraine international having not been involved in competitive football since November 2024. That was via his last appearance in a Conference League win away at Heidenheim in which he scored and then disappeared following his failed test.

Another option this summer would be to send Mudryk on loan to Strasbourg, their sister side in France’s Ligue 1. That would allow him to stay under the BlueCo umbrella.

Coventry City, managed by Frank Lampard, who worked with Mudryk at Stamford Bridge in 2023, are believed to be among those to have enquired, sources have told Daily Mail Sport

View this post on Instagram

Wingers are in-demand in this window, which may explain why so many sides are intrigued by Mudryk’s comeback, despite nobody knowing his current fitness levels. His potential was once considered so highly that Chelsea paid £89million to sign him from Shakhtar Donetsk.

Mudryk is effectively a bonus arrival for Chelsea, with Alonso having told reporters after their pre-season loss to Tottenham in Sydney how the news came as a pleasant surprise. He is set to train under Alonso and with the Chelsea squad in Hong Kong, where the club will be facing Juventus in a friendly.

They also have games in Indonesia and Malaysia which will follow, and will be hosting Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge after returning home to London.

If Mudryk was deemed ready to appear in that match, it would represent his first appearance at the Bridge since facing Arsenal in the Premier League there in November 2024. Chelsea beat Mikel Arteta’s club to secure his signature in January 2023.

Mudryk’s return to football was made possible because of a change in the way the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) measures meldonium – the substance for which he tested positive.

WADA increased the threshold by which a player is deemed to have passed the minimum reporting level, from 120 to 150 per cent. In other words, were Mudryk’s sample analysed today, he would not have been deemed to have violated the anti-doping rules.

Mudryk has now managed to come to a resolution with WADA and the Football Association, in which it has essentially been deemed he has served his time for his violation.

He has spent his suspension – described as long and lonely by sources – training almost daily in the hope of returning. That includes renting the pitch at the stadium of non-League side Uxbridge to stage sessions with a private trainer. Chelsea have been highly sympathetic to Mudryk’s situation, having believed his consistent claims of innocence ever since he tested positive.

It was believed to have occurred while he was away with the Ukraine national team in September 2024, and it was after facing Heidenheim in November 2024 that he was informed of his failed test.

Sports.title: England and Wales withdraw support for Gianni Infantino's re-election as FIFA president - days after his plan to sell the World Cup was scuppered
Sports.content:
England will join Wales by withdrawing their letter of support for Gianni Infantino's re-election as FIFA president.

Wales stuck their head above the parapet and became the first nation to explicitly stand against Infantino's re-election as FIFA president on Monday morning.

The Finnish FA have also revoked their support, with more UEFA nations expected to follow after the confederation itself lost confidence.

And now Daily Mail Sport understands the English FA are sending a letter to Infantino, informing the Swiss football administrator that he no longer has their support.

The FA had already articulated their position on Saturday, releasing a statement calling for change at the top of FIFA and declaring a loss of confidence in Infantino.

Withdrawing letters of support is largely symbolic, as associations had already made it clear that Infantino no longer has their support.

However, it does formally reiterate to Infantino that his position is perilous.

The FA had backed Infantino at every opportunity since his initial election in 2016 and were supporting his re-election bid until plans to sell stakes in the World Cup came to light.

His future is now under intense scrutiny after plans to sell a £3.1billion stake in the World Cup to private investors were revealed by The Times.

Those proposals have since been scrapped after opposition from UEFA, the North, Central America and Caribbean confederation (CONCACAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC).

But as of July, Infantino had reportedly been endorsed by almost all of FIFA's 211 member associations for re-election. Candidates must be put forward by November 18 and the vote will take place at FIFA's congress in March.

'The Football Association of Wales hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr. Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027–2031 term,' a statement from the Welsh FA reads.

'The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr. Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football. Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.'

Wales have become the first nation to withdraw their support for Gianni Infantino's FIFA re-election

Infantino had wanted to sell stakes in the World Cup and FIFA competitions to private investors

He hoped to create a new enterprise with significant investment from Joshua Kushner (pictured) - brother of Jared, Donald Trump's son-in-law

Infantino has been FIFA president since 2016 after replacing Sepp Blatter and is targeting a fourth term in charge.

But the events of recent days - and the controversies that blighted him before and during the World Cup - have rocked his authority.

His plans have been widely lambasted, including by prime minister Andy Burnham, and two of his closest allies have resigned. Firstly, his senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro stepped down before chief operating officer Kevin Lamour lambasted the proposals.

UEFA and CONCACAF have called on Infantino to quit but their ploy to depose the Swiss football administrator hit a roadblock after Kuwait, Qatar, Sri Lanka and Lebanon reiterated their confidence in his leadership.

UEFA and CONCACAF make up 90 of FIFA's 211 member associations. Although that is above the 20 per cent threshold to trigger a vote of no confidence, it falls short of the majority needed to topple Infantino.

With Infantino retaining support from Africa while South America are expected to take the same position, AFC members would be required to oust the FIFA president.

New Zealand could join Europe and CONCACAF's resistance, but it is doubtful that the remaining 10 members of the Oceania Football Confederation would follow suit.

Infantino wrote to all FIFA nations claiming they would receive £30million if they back his plan to sell off stakes in FIFA's major competitions.

Join the discussion Should football's biggest tournaments ever be open to private investment and ownership?

Carlos Cordeiro (left) quit as an advisor to Gianni Infantino (centre) on Friday

The specific proposal was to sell stakes in the tournament to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared. In that light, Infantino's sycophantic behaviour towards Trump - including handing him the inaugural FIFA Peace Price - looks even more suspect.

After his schemes were exposed to the public - very few individuals had known about them - Infantino initially blamed the media for misconstruing them. He has since reneged on his machinations - for now at least.

UEFA welcomed Infantino's abandonment of his plans, writing: 'UEFA welcomes FIFA's decision to withdraw its plan to sell a stake in its competitions - including the World Cup - into private hands.

'The proposal was unanimously rejected by UEFA's national associations and by many other federations and confederations of all sizes around the world, whose job it is to protect football.

'We cannot keep going on like this with secret schemes on fast-track timescales, cooked up by faceless individuals and of dubious benefit to the game. We must identify those responsible and hold them to account.

'It is right that, in the coming days and weeks, UEFA will work with its associations and in close cooperation with other confederations to reflect on how this happened and devise a plan to make sure that it cannot occur again.

'That review should be thorough and fundamental. No option should be off the table. The current FIFA leadership has not only lost UEFA's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family.

'The shabby, back-room, opaque deal he hatched and tried to force through was anything but transparent. This is a victory for the whole game. But it must not be the end of the story. The proposal has gone. The task of rebuilding trust in FIFA has only just begun.'

FIFA president Infantino pictured with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024; UEFA have strongly opposed Infantino's plot

Countless European nations, including England, Wales, the Netherlands and Norway, endorsed the statement.

A spokeswoman for the English FA added: 'We fully support UEFA's position. It is time for a full and robust review of FIFA's leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.'

CONCACAF, as they have all week, followed suit: 'CONCACAF and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

'The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week.

'At a moment that demanded principled leadership, our members stood together in defence of football's long-term interests and the principles of good governance. That unity has prevailed.

'A proposal of this magnitude does not reach that stage by accident. It is a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first.

'This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour. A full review of this leadership must now take place.

'This concern is not CONCACAF's alone. It is shared across many confederations, Member Associations and those who serve and love the game.

'When people entrusted with protecting the game conclude they can no longer do so from within, the football family is entitled to ask how such a proposal was allowed to proceed, and who bears responsibility for it.'

Infantino has since said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.

'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

It remains to be seen what happens to the FIFA president, with Infantino having previously been expected to run unopposed in the governing body's elections next March.

That may change now, while FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations. For context, UEFA have 55 members.

Wales have made the first step.

Sports.title: New Arsenal star CHRISTOS TZOLIS hopes to emulate his hero Alexis Sanchez - and reveals how difficult spell at Norwich shaped his career
Sports.content:
Christos Tzolis vowed ‘now it’s my time’ after previously struggling in England at Norwich as he looks to emulate his childhood Arsenal idol Alexis Sanchez.

The 24-year-old winger joined the Gunners in a £34million transfer from Club Bruges last month, where he struck an extraordinary 40 goal contributions (17 goals, 23 assists) in 36 league appearances last season.

It’s a steep trajectory from his struggles at Norwich in the Premier League five years ago. He failed to breakthrough, before going on loan spells to FC Twente and Fortuna Dusseldorf — and then making the switch to Belgium.

Though Tzolis feels as though he is now a completely transformed player from the one who last played in the English top-flight.

He said: ‘It was totally different than now. It's always difficult for a team that is promoted from the second division to the Premier League to play high level football.

‘The team I think was not really ready for the Premier League and that makes it also difficult for me to adapt and to play how I could.

Christos Tzolis believes he is a transformed play as he returns to the Premier League with Arsenal

The £34million signing from Club Bruges believes he has similarities to his idol Alexis Sanchez, who starred at Arsenal during four years in North London

‘You can have some setbacks and difficulties. I only learnt a lot of things from this period at Norwich.

‘I have three years in a row that I’m important for my teams and I have a big role in an attacking part. And I feel now more ready to be in the Premier League. Now I have the chance to play for Arsenal. For me, I think I did the right decision after Norwich. I developed myself, I improved a lot. I’m not the same player I was in Norwich, 100 per cent.

‘I feel it also in my body and also in my mindset. Now it’s my time to show that I’m ready and capable of playing in the Premier League.’

He has hit the ground running upon joining Arsenal less than two weeks ago, marking his full debut for the club against Girona on Saturday with a first goal. The winger received the ball on the left before cutting inside and firing his shot into the bottom-right corner via a deflection off Kai Havertz.

Tzolis wears the No17 shirt, which was once donned by his idol Sanchez. He sees similarities between himself and the ex-Gunners forward, who became one of Arsenal’s standout stars during his four years in north London.

‘Actually, I knew that he (Sanchez) was wearing the shirt of number 17,’ said Tzolis. ‘Of course, I watched a lot of football and he was a top player for Arsenal, as a left winger always. He’s one of the players I looked up to when I was younger. And also, I see some similarities with him. But it’s not the reason I took the number 17.

‘It’s nice (though). Alexis Sanchez had number 17 — so I hope I will have the same success.’

He’s certainly already making up for lost time having quickly become the man to beat in fitness tests, according to Ben White.

The England man remarked: ‘Christos has been amazing. He came in, did all the testing, and beat everyone. So he is fitting in really well and everyone is really happy for him to be here.’

Tzolis struggled to make a breakthrough in the Premier League while at Norwich, but has since enjoyed a steep rise leading to champion Arsenal signing him this summer

The Greek winger scored on his first appearance in an Arsenal shirt in their friendly with Girona

Tzolis wholeheartedly agreed. He means business.

‘I know I've won so far,’ he added. ‘There are not all the players here. There are still some players that have to do the tests, of course.

‘But so far I'm first in the fitness test. It's like 20 metres, go back, 40 metres, go back, 60 metres, go back, I think five times in a row. So it's around 1.2k and it's as fast as possible. Actually, it's pretty hard.

‘Actually I had the advantage that I started pre-season also with Bruges so I was already training for two weeks and always I wanted to keep myself fit during summer so I was ready.

‘I came here ready (with) my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well.’

Sports.title: Non-league club confirm 'humble and generous' Jadon Sancho trained at their ground - just three miles from Man United's Carrington training base - as £73m star awaits his next move after leaving Old Trafford as a free agent
Sports.content:
Non-league club confirm 'humble and generous' Jadon Sancho trained at their ground - just three miles from Man United's Carrington training base - as £73m star awaits his next move after leaving Old Trafford as a free agent

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jadon Sancho has been waiting out a decision over his future training at a non-league ground, the club has confirmed.

Manchester United's former £73million man departed Old Trafford this summer as a free agent after a checkered five-year stint.

But as he ponders his next move, Sancho opted for an unorthodox venue to keep fit - 10th-tier side Flixton FC, with the 26-year-old visiting and then training at their 2,000 Valley Ground.

The ground is just three miles from Man United's storied training ground Carrington, but a world away, as the home to members of the North West Counties League Division One North.

Sancho's appearance at the non-league side came as such a surprise that Flixton were forced to release a statement explaining why he had chosen the ground, and praising his 'humble' nature.

'Over the past few days, we've seen a number of posts and comments circulating regarding Jadon Sancho's visit to Flixton FC,' the statement began. 'To clarify, Jadon was not on trial with the club and was not involved in any transfer discussions.

View this post on Instagram

Non-league side Flixton FC have released a statement after Jadon Sancho visited the club and trained at its ground

The former Manchester United star has not yet decided who he will continue his career with

'He simply used our facilities for a private training session to maintain his fitness while preparing for the next chapter of his career.

'We're proud that the quality of our pitch and facilities made Flixton a place where a player of his caliber felt comfortable training, and he is welcome to train at Flixton FC whenever he wishes.

'During his visit, Jadon was nothing but professional, humble, and generous with his time. After completing his session, he happily met with young supporters, posed for photos, signed autographs, and left a lasting impression on everyone who had the pleasure of meeting him.

'Jadon is a world-class footballer who has achieved more in the game than most players could ever dream of. He deserves respect for both his accomplishments and the way he conducted himself during his visit, not the unwarranted criticism that has followed.

'We thank Jadon for choosing Flixton FC as a place to train and wish him every success in the next stage of his career, which will undoubtedly be at a level far above where we currently compete. Our doors will always be open for him.'

Sancho had been a long-desired signing under former Man United manager Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, finally arriving at Old Trafford in the summer of 2021.

But after an uneven first two seasons peppered with injury, Sancho underwent a punishing exile at the start of the 2023-24 season after falling out of favour with then-manager Erik ten Hag.

Sancho had seemingly hit out at his head coach after Ten Hag had said publicly that he had not made the squad to face Arsenal due to his performances in training not being to his manager's liking.

The player spent nearly six months away from competitive action before a loan to his former club Borussia Dortmund in January 2024.

Season-long stints at Chelsea and Aston Villa followed, with Sancho in May becoming the first player in history to make three European finals, in three consecutive seasons, in three different cup competitions, for three different clubs.

But despite bursts of promise, Sancho still has no confirmed destination for the start of the coming season.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that Qatari side Al-Rayyan were keeping tabs on the former England international, with Atletico Madrid also maintaining an interest in the star.

Sports.title: Manchester United Women part company with head coach Marc Skinner - as pressure mounts on club to keep pace with WSL rivals
Sports.content:
Manchester United Women have reached a mutual agreement with head coach Marc Skinner to terminate his contract, ending his five-year tenure at the club.

Skinner departs having overseen the most successful period in the team's history, guiding United to three consecutive Women's FA Cup finals, including lifting the trophy in 2024 with a 4-0 victory over Tottenham at Wembley in front of a sold-out crowd.

The win secured the club's first major honour, although United were beaten by Chelsea in the 2023 and 2025 finals.

Skinner also led United to their highest-ever Women's Super League finish in 2022-23, when they ended the campaign as runners-up and qualified for the Women's Champions League for the first time.

The 48-year-old signed a new two-year contract last summer, with the option of a further year, after securing a second consecutive Champions League qualification place.

However, his final season in charge proved a disappointing one as an injury-hit squad fell short on multiple fronts. United finished fourth in the WSL behind champions Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City, missing out on Champions League qualification.

Manchester United Women manager Marc Skinner has reached a mutual agreement with the club to terminate his contract after five years in charge

The 48-year-old led United to three consecutive Women's FA Cup finals, lifting the trophy in 2024 to secure the club's first major honour

They also lost the League Cup final to Chelsea and saw their maiden European campaign in the competition proper end in the quarter-finals against Bayern Munich.

A statement from the club read: 'Marc leaves having made a significant contribution to the continued progress of Manchester United Women.

'The club places on record its sincere thanks for his professionalism, commitment and dedication throughout his time at United, and wishes him every success in the future.'

Skinner's departure comes at a time when questions are growing over whether United are investing enough to compete with the Women's Super League's leading clubs.

While rivals have strengthened significantly this summer, United have made just two signings: 22-year-old defender Andrea Medina and 27-year-old goalkeeper Janina Leitzig. They have also lost star forward Melvine Malard to Chelsea in a deal reportedly worth around £850,000.

London City Lionesses, who finished fifth last season, have signed two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas, while Lyon defender Alice Sombath, who lifted the Champions League with the French side in 2022, has joined Tottenham. Arsenal have strengthened with the additions of Lionesses midfielder Georgia Stanway and World Cup-winning right back Ona Battle and Chelsea have added experience in Katie McCabe and Malard. Man City have signed England's Euro-winning pair Beth Mead and Niamh Charles.

Throughout his tenure, Skinner has faced criticism from sections of the fanbase, with some arguing he has taken the team as far as he can.

For some, last season's runs to the League Cup final and Champions League quarter-finals only reinforced that view, with critics arguing United cannot get over the line in the biggest games. Their record of one win from four finals - with all three defeats coming against Chelsea - adds weight to this argument.

The former Birmingham City and Orlando Pride manager, however, consistently pointed to the gap in investment between United and their closest rivals, insisting the club risked standing still as others accelerated.

'We see the investment around us, we see the strategy around us,' he said in May.

'No longer can we just look at them teams above us, we have to be able to be aware of those teams below.

'I know everybody wants to jump on the negative but there's also amazing growth from this team too. We have to do some reflection, of course we do.

'The reality is we have to assess over the summer where the resource goes and which direction we push that in, to make sure we stay in that chasing pack and obviously make sure the teams behind us can't catch us.'

Skinner departs with just over a month until United begin the new Women's Super League season away to London City Lionesses on September 4.

Sports.title: Liverpool stance over sale of Cody Gakpo made clear amid interest from Tottenham - as highly-rated Reds academy star attracts interest from EFL clubs
Sports.content:
Liverpool stance over sale of Cody Gakpo made clear amid interest from Tottenham - as highly-rated Reds academy star attracts interest from EFL clubs

Read more on this deal and the latest transfer news in our dedicated WINDOW WATCH

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Liverpool have no plans to sell Cody Gakpo despite Tottenham making their interest in the forward known.

The Reds, who continue to work on a deal for Paris Saint-Germain's £145million-rated Bradley Barcola, are looking to add attacking quality rather than lose it.

Gakpo, 27, is contracted until 2030 and with current market prices escalating for players of his experience, it would take a huge sum to change Liverpool's stance.

The Dutchman had a weaker season than usual last time out, scoring only nine goals, but is highly valued by Liverpool all the same. His best season, 2024-25, saw him bang in 18 goals.

Liverpool have already lost Mohamed Salah this summer and their only attacking arrival has been winger Víctor Munoz from Osasuna for £34.5million.

They paid PSV £44m for Gakpo in 2022.

Tottenham want to get their hands on Cody Gakpo - but Liverpool have no intention to sell him

Tottenham are also keeping a watching brief on Omar Marmoush at Manchester City as well as negotiating for Savinho.

Spurs have so far set about strengthening their defence and midfield.

Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka has arrived from Burnley on a free, while they have also picked up defenders Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi for nothing from Liverpool and Bournemouth respectively.

Their marquee defensive purchase has been Jan Paul van Hecke, for whom they paid Brighton £52m.

In midfield, they have signed Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100m and Mateus Fernandes from relegated West Ham for £85m.

Signing World Cup star Gakpo could, therefore, take Roberto De Zerbi's summer spend close to or even beyond £300m.

Meanwhile, Liverpool forward Keyrol Figueroa is attracting interest from Barnsley and Salford.

The 19-year-old impressed for the U21s during their recent camp in Slovakia, and scored in a friendly against Cardiff on Saturday.

Defender Wellity Lucky made a return from injury at the weekend, and will also be loaned out. Cardiff want Liverpool left-back Calum Scanlon on loan.

Sports.title: Liverpool's second-half changes exposed Andoni Iraola's blunt attack but the new boss MUST give starts to two teenagers - while Daniel Farke faces a huge call as Leeds aim to make a big push
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola was left with plenty to ponder as he jetted back across the Atlantic after his Liverpool side blew a two-goal lead to be well beaten by Leeds in Chicago.

In the Reds’ final game of this pre-season tour, early goals from young defender Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz had Liverpool on their way to a perfect trip but, after both teams made half-time changes, Leeds vastly improved to triumph.

At the home of NFL side Chicago Bears, two American football-style throw-ins undid Liverpool as Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored a brace. Joe Rodon and Sean Longstaff also bagged for Daniel Farke’s side as Leeds bombarded the penalty area with set-pieces.

Liverpool throw it away

This was a game worthy of the dictionary definition for the old ‘game of two halves’ cliche.

When Wirtz, Isak, Ngumoha and Nyoni went off, Liverpool had nothing going forward. Likewise, the half-time introductions of Calvert-Lewin, Harry Wilson et al gave Leeds the spark that was missing.

But it was two Hail Mary-style throw-ins that propelled Leeds to victory. Shrewd runs off the ball from Calvert-Lewin, abysmal defending from Liverpool. Given the Reds’ set-piece frailties last season, it is a glaringly obvious area to improve.

It does not help that several senior defenders are injured, with Jeremie Frimpong limping off in the second half. The Dutchman’s issue is the fifth in the back four with Joe Gomez, Conor Bradley, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni all out – and captain Virgil van Dijk not on this trip.

Liverpool threw away a 2-0 lead against Leeds in their final match of their pre-season tour

Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored a brace for Leeds as the Reds collapsed after half-time

Florian Wirtz had scored a fine goal but the Reds had no attacking threat when he and others went off

Two teenagers push for starts

Rio Ngumoha is so talented that, in the eyes of many, he is not counted as one of the kids looking to break through any more.

It is easy to forget he is still just 17. This time last year, he was yet to make his Premier League debut.

Now, it would be a surprise if Ngumoha, capped by England in a pre-World Cup friendly, did not start the first game of the upcoming season.

Liverpool are trying to sign Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola but that should not halt Ngumoha’s meteoric rise.

The winger is ready for the next step, which is playing more often after five league starts last term. He terrorised wing back James Justin here.

The breakout star of this tour, though, has been another teenager: Trey Nyoni. The 19-year-old made six substitute appearances in the league last term but is ready for more.

Midfielder Nyoni has bossed players ten years his senior on this tour, dictating play from deep. He is small in stature but can be a giant for Iraola in the coming years.

With Alexis Mac Allister still absent after making the World Cup final with Argentina, Ryan Gravenberch only just back and Curtis Jones the subject of interest in a move away, is Nyoni’s time now?

Still just 17, it would be a surprise if Rio Ngumoha did not start Liverpool's season opener

It could be Trey Nyoni's time, meanwhile, with the 19-year-old shining while on tour

Should Farke stick or twist with the winning formula?

Farke was sleep-walking towards the sack as Christmas approached last year, with Leeds in the relegation zone with a run of six defeats in the seven games.

But the boss changed formation to a back five and, from December 1 onwards, Leeds only lost six of 25 matches and got to an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke is not a negative coach by nature and the stubborn system may be unnatural but the signs are that he is set to stick by it.

The verdict here in Illinois? In the first half, it was worrying: they looked vulnerable at the back and created very little on the counter-attack.

After the break and a quadruple change – but the same system – they looked in fine fettle and played Liverpool off the park. The exercise will prompt both managers to know their best XIs.

Leeds could make a push – with a few more signings

Leeds were ten times better after the break.

With James Trafford expected to become their record signing for around £45million, this could be a window that gives Leeds a platform for a top-half push, especially after tempting Wilson to join on a free transfer from Fulham.

However, they are still light in some positions. Gabriel Gudmundsson limping off in the first half highlighted left back as a problem area, while the forward line could do with being strengthened after missing out on Julian Brandt and seeing Jack Harrison depart.

New £34million defender Tarik Muharemovic looks a solid buy from Sassuolo to replace Pascal Struijk.

Leeds could push for a top-half finish if they pick up a few more summer signings

Wirtz in full Flo already

Wirtz and Alexander Isak both struggled to live up to hopes or expectations last season due to fitness and form issues.

Arne Slot had many issues but the Dutchman might have had better success if he had been able to call upon a fully fit-and-firing version of the duo, who cost £241million combined.

Both are back with a point to prove now, though – and new boss Iraola knows he too will be unable to achieve his ambitions without these two on song.

On their first pre-season outings after a post-World Cup break, both looked sharp. Wirtz took his goal nicely and also played some gasp-inducing passes, while Isak seemed to be full of confidence. The second-half fall-off shows their importance.

Sports.title: Furious UEFA warned Gianni Infantino NOT to destroy botched World Cup plan documents with lawsuit threatened before FIFA president abandoned his plot
Sports.content:
UEFA threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action on Friday over his botched plan to sell off the World Cup to private investors.

The FIFA president was forced to abandon a hugely controversial proposal to sell stakes in the tournament to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, on Saturday, following a major revolt from the footballing world.

That heaped the pressure on Infantino, with UEFA subsequently declaring a loss of confidence in the Italian-Swiss administrator.

European football's governing body had previously led the rebellion, announcing on Thursday that their 55 member nations would boycott the World Cup if the plans weren't scrapped.

And now, UEFA threatened to go to court over the scheme, which was known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), in a letter they sent to Infantino on Friday.

The report adds that UEFA also wrote to Kushner, Greg Maffei, J.P. Morgan and OpenEconomics, and said they were 'actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints' as a result of the collapsed proposal.

UEFA reportedly threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action over his botched World Cup plan

FIFA president Infantino pictured with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024

The letter to Infantino read: 'Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below.

'You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.'

UEFA went on to warn FIFA that 'any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment or loss of relevant materials' after their letter 'may constitute spoliation of evidence'.

They then refused to rule out further action if any of the aforementioned actions took place, but the letter itself is not legal action.

The letter also insisted that FIFA must ensure that certain individuals, including Infantino, Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and Kevin Lamour, FIFA's chief operating officer, 'specifically preserve all such materials in their possession'.

UEFA confirmed to Daily Mail Sport that a document preservation letter was sent.

Kushner was expected to lead the proposed investor group through his Thrive Eternal fund, while Maffei, who is a Trump donor, was also set to be involved.

J.P. Morgan and OpenEconomics were involved in the search for investors.

UEFA also wrote to Joshua Kushner, who was expected to lead the group of private investors

Speaking on Saturday as he announced the abandonment of his plans, Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.'

He continued: 'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marked an embarrassing u-turn for Infantino, given it came less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans and blamed the media for misconstruing them.

It remains to be seen what happens to the FIFA president, with Infantino having previously been expected to run unopposed in the governing body's elections next March.

That may change now, while FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations. For context, UEFA have 55 members.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua's future questioned after win - 'Does he belong in the ring?'
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua's future questioned after win - 'Does he belong in the ring?'

Anthony Joshua was dropped twice against Kristian Prenga last month before recovering to stop the Albanian and set up a clash with Tyson Fury

View Image Anthony Joshua was dropped twice (Image: Richard Pelham/Getty Images)

Lennox Lewis has questioned whether Anthony Joshua should still be fighting.

‌



Joshua returned to action last month in his first fight since he walked away from a car crash which killed two of his best friends last Christmas. Joshua was dropped twice in the opening round by Kristian Prenga before stopping the Albanian in the second round to set up his belated clash with Tyson Fury.

‌



But former heavyweight world champion Lewis doubts whether Joshua should carry on competing. "Does he really belong in the ring right now?" he told The Ring. "A virtual novice put him on the ground twice in the first round. Is that it, have we seen the last of him? It's not like he's his old self."

‌



Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua told exactly how he can beat Tyson Fury READ MORE :

The night before Joshua's comeback win, Fury stopped Mariusz Wach in his own warm-up fight. Joshua and Fury signed contracts earlier this year but no date or venue has been announced. And Lewis believes Fury is in now in pole position to win a fight which has been a decade in the making.

"I think Fury boxes to the level of his opposition," he added. "He's trying to keep sharp for Joshua, the right thing to do, and needed to have a tick-over fight. Him going some more rounds in his legs is what he wanted and did, so just a warm-up for another fight. Obviously, this has turned into a money thing. The fight should have happened [years ago], but they want to make the fight, and can make some money out of it. You can't say either is at their best now.

Article continues below

"Fury is closer but both are shadows of their former selves. I'd side with Fury ... he showed me more in his two fights [against Arslanbek Makhmudov and Wach] than Joshua has recently. He boxed a YouTuber [Jake Paul], now boxed a guy who knocked him down twice and next faces Fury? That's a big step up."

Sports.title: Sir Chris Hoy hails 'miracle drug' behind terminal prostate cancer fight
Sports.content:
Sir Chris Hoy hails 'miracle drug' behind terminal prostate cancer fight

The former six-time Olympic track cycling champion, Sir Chris Hoy, revealed that his prostate cancer diagnosis was terminal back in October 2024

View 2 Images Sir Chris Hoy at the Commonwealth Games (Image: Karwai Tang)

Sir Chris Hoy has spoken about the positive effect exercise has had in his battle with terminal prostate cancer, claiming it would be "hailed as a miracle drug" if it were in pill form.

‌



The six-time Olympic cycling champion, 50, revealed back in September 2023 that he had been diagnosed with cancer. In October 2024, Hoy shared the news that the disease had spread to his bones and that he had been given two to four years to live.

‌



Hoy recently made an appearance at the Commonwealth Games, where he provided track cycling analysis for TNT Sports.

‌



And the former champion cycler has spoken about how exercise has helped him since his diagnosis. He told The Big Issue: “Exercise is a big part of my dealing with my cancer. There’s numerous studies to show that exercise can improve the efficacy of the cancer medications. It can improve your time to relapse.

“If it was in pill form, it would be hailed as a miracle drug.

“Actually, for my diagnosis, it took a long time to find any positivity or opportunity from that really difficult situation. For me, that was saying maybe we can change attitudes to Stage 4 cancer.”

‌



Hoy has shown tremendous courage speaking openly about his diagnosis, including when he shared the news that the disease had reached Stage 4.

In the same interview, he said that he didn't want to give off the impression that he had "cracked it", admitting that he has good and bad days in his battle against cancer.

View 2 Images Hoy was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2023 (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Article continues below

“One thing I would say is, don’t expect to feel positive and great all the time. You don’t go in the gym once, pick up a dumbbell and go, ‘Well, that’s me strong now.’

“The mental side of a cancer diagnosis is probably the biggest challenge by far. The physical side is difficult, but the mental side is the real challenge.

“I don’t want to present myself as someone doing really well, everything’s great, I’ve cracked it. There are some days where it’s really tough. There are ups and downs. You can get through the most difficult of moments if you bring yourself back to the here and now, and don’t try and think too far ahead.”

Sports.title: Donald Trump faces cheating allegations again after winning another golf tournament
Sports.content:
Donald Trump faces cheating allegations again after winning another golf tournament

Donald Trump has been accused of cheating, with social media users raising questions about footage of the US president's 'winning shot'

View 2 Images Donald Trump's golf exploits haven't convinced everyone (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

United States president Donald Trump has faced fresh allegations of cheating on the golf course after his latest triumph. The claims from sport fans come after the 80-year-old's success at the Bedminster Club Championship.

‌



Trump, currently serving his second presidential term, has long been a keen golfer. This has sometimes brought him criticism from those who worry he has shown more dedication to this pastime than to his political office - in 2025, it was estimated that he had spent around 25 per cent of his days in office out on the course during his second presidential term.

‌



Not only does the president play a lot of golf, he also owns a number of courses in the States and further afield. It was at one of these courses, Trump National Bedminster in New Jersey, where his latest victory arrived.

‌



Trump claimed to have won with a score of 70, sharing footage of an apparent winning shot on his social media platform Truth Social. “I won with a score of 70, and am so honoured in that, unlike the rest of the field, I’m given very little time to practice, because I’m focused on many other things. It’s called TALENT, and I have it, and they don’t!” he wrote.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Harry Kane describes 'surreal' golf game with Donald Trump ahead of England vs Norway READ MORE :

Donald Trump denied Masters club membership as golf legend opens up on quitting TV job READ MORE :

The commander-in-chief frequently boasts about his prowess on the course and previously claimed to have won club and senior championships in Florida in 2024. Trump National Golf Club Bedminster plays to a par of 72, indicating a two under par final round for the politician, though not everyone was convinced by the achievement.

‌



"I've seen his swing, he didn't shoot 70 unless he cheated and played from the short tees. No way," one social media claimed. Another wrote: "It's funny that he cheats to win and knows this. But he doesn't care. He just wants to win by whatever means.

"Watched him live for years, listened to his caddies stories. Everyone around him allows him to cheat out of fear. Nothing he does is genuine. All his 'feats' are fake, and he actually feels special," a third cynic argued, while a fourth claimed to have seen footage of the president's caddie moving the ball for him.

View 2 Images Trump owns a number of golf courses as well as being a keen player himself (Image: TIMOTHY A. CLARY, AFP via Getty Images)

‌



On a video shared by Trump of him playing the 'winning shot' at the Bedminster Club Championship, further users raised questions over the footage, which depicted a ball delicately chipped onto the green and coming to a halt close to the hole. "Lol 100% that golf ball is remote controlled! those bounces are not normal," one wrote.

"That ball had a string : ) or front brakes," another suggested. There was even a separate allegation of "A little helpful foot tap at some point by someone."

Others pointed out that the ball never actually dropped into the hole, as Trump is well known for conceding putts when the ball is considered close enough. One user wrote: "Did it 'automatically' count as 'going in the hole'? Just being in the general area?".

Article continues below

Trump is a passionate golfer who has faced fierce criticism for spending a considerable portion of his second presidential term out on the course. Trump also owns courses in Scotland and was spotted playing a round during a recent visit to the UK.

Some still remain sceptical about his golfing prowess. Trump's consistency on the course and incredible record have been questioned, with sports columnist Rick Reilly accusing him of cheating in the past, saying: "When it comes to cheating, he's an 11 on a scale of one to 10."

Sports.title: Wales become first country to withdraw Gianni Infantino support as pressure grows on FIFA chief
Sports.content:
Wales become first country to withdraw Gianni Infantino support as pressure grows on FIFA chief

A football association from the UK has become the first to officially withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election next March, days after he U-turned on plans to 'sell off' the World Cup

View 3 Images Infantino is under pressure (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

A British football association has become the first FIFA member to officially pull its support for Gianni Infantino's re-election.

‌



The move is set to heap pressure on the Italian, who faces a severe backlash over his plans 'sell off' the World Cup. Even after cancelling the project, set to be led by a close Donald Trump ally, the FIFA President is rapidly losing support from major players in the game.

‌



The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has now reportedly made its position clear and written to FIFA to withdraw its support for Infantino's re-election.

‌



The FAW also backed a boycott of FIFA competitions orchestrated by European governing body, UEFA, in response to Infantino's plan to create a private company, open to investment, to run its headline competitions to raise billions of pounds.

5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job READ MORE :

It was reportedly going to be led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law. After Infantino’s plans were revealed by the media, before some high-ranking FIFA officials were even informed of his intentions, he faced a severe backlash.

UEFA, the organisation which runs European football, said it would boycott FIFA competitions until the plans were killed, and CONCACAF, its North American counterpart, also criticised the plans. Key advisers to Infantino also resigned in protest.

‌



View 3 Images Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump. (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Italian Infantino is due for re-election in March, but his future at the top of world football looks in doubt after this latest scandal.

Now, the FAW has heaped pressure on his tenure, officially withdrawing its support for Infantino’s re-election, according to reports.

‌



The association told Sky News it "hereby confirms its withdrawal of support for the candidature of Mr Gianni Infantino, for re-election as FIFA President for the 2027-2031 term.

"The recent failures in good governance, processes, leadership, values, stakeholder management, communications and sound judgement have led us to a position where Mr Infantino has lost the confidence of the FAW to remain at the helm of world football.

View 3 Images Wales failed to qualify for the 2026 World Cup, but did appear at Qatar 2022 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



"Failing to put the best interests of football first is a failure we cannot accept.

“The Football Association of Wales has written to FIFA to inform them of their position.”

Other British football associations are yet to follow suit, but all approved the UEFA boycott. However, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has gone one step further and said Infantino is ‘the wrong man’ to lead FIFA.

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer need brutally exposed as Leeds stun Andoni Iraola - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 2-4 LEEDS UNITED: Daniel Farke's men scored four goals in 25 second-half minutes to stun the Reds and win in the Premier League Summer Series on Sunday

View 3 Images Leeds United beat Liverpool 4-2 on Sunday as they mounted a stunning comeback (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool were left stunned as Leeds United produced a scintillating second-half comeback to come from 2-0 down and beat the Reds 4-2 in the Premier League Super Series.

‌



Fresh off the back of beating Sunderland and Championship side Wrexham, Andoni Iraola's side started on the front foot against Leeds and opened the scoring inside the first seven minutes. Luke Chambers was the goalscorer for the Reds as he smashed home from close range.

‌



Although Leeds did have some opportunities, Liverpool controlled most of the first half and ended up doubling their advantage just before the break. Florian Wirtz found the net for Iraola's side, as he finished off an excellent team move, tucking the ball home into the corner.

‌



Both teams made four substitutions at half-time and it was Leeds who came out as the stronger after the break. Brendan Aaronson capitalised on a mistake to pull one back for Daniel Farke's side on the hour mark, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised with a finish from inside the box.

The comeback was then complete soon after with Sean Longstaff firing home following some neat play from Aaronson. Calvert-Lewin added his second and Leeds' fourth late on to ensure the Whites were crowned as the winners of the 2026 Premier League Summer Series in the United States.

Liverpool handed Bradley Barcola transfer boost as PSG strike contingency plan READ MORE :

Mirror Football looks at the big talking points from the game...

‌



Fast Liverpool start

Liverpool scored the first goal in each of their first two pre-season friendlies and that theme continued against Leeds. Chambers, who has come into central defence since Joe Gomez suffered a new muscle injury in the 4-2 win over Sunderland last week, was the man who gave the Reds the lead.

Dominik Szoboszlai's outswinging corner was flicked on by Milos Kerkez and Chambers was there free inside the box to slam home from eight yards. In truth, it was a smart finish from the 22-year-old, who could have easily got underneath the ball but he kept his head over it before lashing beyond goalkeeper Alex Cairns.

View 3 Images Florian Wirtz scored for Liverpool against Leeds (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Huge Leeds injury blow

One of Daniel Farke's main wishes going into the fixture against Liverpool would have been to avoid any fresh injuries with three weeks to go until the start of the Premier League season. Well, unfortunately for him and the Whites Gabriel Gudmundsson hobbled off with what looked like a hamstring problem.

After going down in the opening stages with a knock, Gudmundsson carried on before being substituted in the 34th minute. The Sweden international went down appearing to hold his hamstring and was treated by the Leeds medical staff before going off and being replaced by Sebastiaan Bornauw.

Impressive Wirtz

Following a mixed first season and Liverpool's lack of attacking transfer business so far this summer, it does feel as though there is some pressure on Wirtz to produce in 2026/27. But the German showed in his first appearance back after the World Cup that he can step up and deliver after scoring the Reds' second against Leeds.

‌



It was well-worked move by Liverpool as Trey Nyoni's cross-field pass found Jeremie Frimpong who cut the ball back for Wirtz to sweep home first time from inside the box. With just seven goals in 49 matches in his debut season at the Reds, Wirtz will be no doubt wanting to improve on that total this term.

View 3 Images Wirtz had an impressive first-half

Liverpool punished for mistake

Although it's much better to iron out mistakes in pre-season, of course, Liverpool won't want to give too many goals like the one Leeds scored against them in Chicago.

‌



Milos Kerkez, who endured a difficult first season at the Reds following his move from Bournemouth last summer, gave the ball away inside his own half and Leeds punished them. Ampadu collected the ball and drove at the Liverpool back-line before playing in Aaronson and he slotted low past Giorgi Mamardashvili. It was a slack piece of play from Kerkez and he must eradicate them if he wants to be a success at Anfield.

Impressive comeback from Leeds

Leeds were much-improved after Calvert-Lewin, Aaronson, Sean Longstaff and Harry Wilson came on at half-time and they produced a scintillating comeback to stun Liverpool.

After Aaronson pulled one back, Calvert-Lewin levelled for the Whites in the 71st minute. A long-throw from Ampadu caused chaos in the box and Joe Rodon's flick-on was hammered home by Calvert-Lewin from close-range.

‌



Then, just two minutes later, the fightback was complete as Leeds took the lead for the first time in the game. Longstaff was the scorer on this occasion for Leeds, as he swivelled inside the area before drilling home.

The Whites would go on to score a fourth goal to seal the win and it came from another long throw. This time it was Bornauw who got the flick on and Calvert-Lewin was there once more to tap home from four yards.

It was an impressive comeback from Leeds and excellent character after falling 2-0 down and looking like the game was over at half-time. But Farke has instilled some belief into his side and it was on show in full flow again.

‌



Liverpool icon tells Reds what they need to win Premier League title READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Fresh Bradley Barcola transfer boost as improved bid to go in for star READ MORE :

Liverpool transfer priorities clear

If it wasn't clear before that Liverpool need to sign some players, it certainly is now. The Reds have got to bring in at least two, if not, three ready-made first-team starters before their Premier League opener against Newcastle United.

They have been among the quietest clubs in the top flight when it comes to signing players this summer and it's seen Iraola's squad look threadbare with Ibrahima Konate, Andy Robertson and Mohamed Salah moving on. Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz have come in, but neither have made an appearance for the Reds so far.

The Reds are so light in a number of areas and the one that looked the weakest against Leeds was the centre-back area. While Jacquet is coming in to join Virgil van Dijk and the returning Giovani Leoni, Gomez's latest injury blow should see Iraola's side dip into the market to sign another central defender. That is a must.

Article continues below

As well as that, the Reds are lacking a serious right winger following Salah's departure, while it does still feel like they need a new left-back to help Kerkez and a high-profile central midfielder.

Sports.title: UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'
Sports.content:
UEFA threaten Gianni Infantino legal action as FIFA chief warned not to 'destroy evidence'

UEFA are reported to have sent a letter to FIFA and its president, Gianni Infantino, as the aftermath of the failed FFE plans continue

View 2 Images UEFA havei issued a legal threat to FIFA president Gianni Infantino (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

UEFA have threatened under-fire FIFA president Gianni Infantino with legal action - and warned him against destroying any documents relating to the failed World Cup ‘sale’ plan.

‌



Controversial news emerged earlier this week that FIFA had plans to sell shares in the organisation's tournaments, which would have included the men’s and women’s World Cups, as well as the Club World Cup. The plans were met with widespread criticism, with UEFA being joined by CONCACAF and AFC in making it clear they were against such plans, which were going to be called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

‌



UEFA, following a meeting with its 55 member associations, threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions if the proposals put forward by the governing body and Infantino went ahead. The backlash eventually led to Infantino releasing a statement which confirmed the controversial scheme was to be scrapped, citing the ‘division’ within football as a reason.

‌



5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

The Telegraph has now claimed to have seen a letter which has been sent by UEFA to FIFA, as well as potential investors Joshua Kushner, Greg Maffei, JP Morgan and OpenEconomics. It has been reported that UEFA has threatened legal action and has warned FIFA not to destroy any evidence relating to the failed FFE proposals.

“Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below,” a letter written by UEFA and seen by the Telegraph, says.

“You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.

‌



“These obligations arise independently of any internal retention policy you or your organisation maintain and supersede any routine document destruction or deletion policies that would otherwise apply.”

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino was forced to perform a dramatic u-turn with the FFE proposals (Image: Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



The letter continued: “Uefa – as well as other confederations, Fifa member associations and football stakeholders – has strongly condemned the FFE plan in the strongest terms as fundamentally incompatible with the proper governance of football.

“Given that proceedings are reasonably anticipated, you are obliged to preserve all relevant materials (as defined below) with immediate effect.”

In another warning to FIFA, UEFA are quoted as adding in the letter: “Uefa puts you on formal notice that any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment, or loss of relevant materials following receipt of this notice – or following any earlier date on which you were, or reasonably should have been, aware that proceedings were anticipated – may constitute spoliation of evidence.

Article continues below

“Uefa reserves all rights to seek appropriate remedies in the proceedings for any such destruction or loss, including applications for adverse inference orders, sanctions, and costs against the responsible party or parties.”

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer 'cancelled' as Andoni Iraola proven right with frustrations after U-turn
Sports.content:
Liverpool transfer 'cancelled' as Andoni Iraola proven right with frustrations after U-turn

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has spoken about his dislike for the month of August due to the uncertainty surrounding transfers and one of his players has changed their mind on a move

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is frustrated by the uncertainty of the transfer window (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Federico Chiesa is set to stay at Liverpool for the 2026/27 season under Andoni Iraola after reportedly deciding against pursuing a transfer.

‌



Chiesa has been a bit-part player during his Liverpool career and had been expected to leave in the summer transfer window. Interest from Serie A and Atletico Madrid, and Liverpool's willingness to sell, had combined to make a move appear likely.

‌



However, the Italian forward has gone on Liverpool's pre-season tour of the United States where he has decided he wants to stay and fight for his place in the side. Calciomercato says this is something of a U-turn from the 28-year-old.

‌



Chiesa has just five goals and five assists in 50 appearances for Liverpool following his £10million move from Juventus two years ago. Just three of his 34 appearances were starts last season under Arne Slot's management and a move elsewhere to find more regular game time had been on the cards. But he has two years remaining on his contract and has reportedly decided to stick rather than twist.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Liverpool spent £35m to sign Victor Munoz from Osasuna and remain in the market for another winger, with Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola among the options after the chances of landing RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande receded.

‌



It has been a largely frustrating start to the summer transfer window for the Reds, with the departure of Fenway Sports Group chief Michael Edwards complicating things.

Iraola was brought in after three impressive seasons at Bournemouth to turn around the disappointing drop-off in Slot's second campaign. And, while the Spaniard has been working hard in pre-season, he has admitted to frustrations around the uncertainty involved in the transfer window.

View 2 Images Federico Chiesa now wants to stay at Liverpool (Image: Bill Barrett/Getty Images)

‌



"I particularly hate this month of August because you start the competition, you still don't know if some of the players are going to leave, who is going to come, there is a lot of uncertainty," Iraola told reporters in Chicago.

"It's difficult to build a proper team with a lot of question marks, but it is what it is, it is the same for all the teams. It is the same every season and I particularly enjoy when it's the first of September - done, this is who we are and we build from here.

"But we have to deal with this month of August that I think a lot of the coaches, if not all, we don't like it."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
