World.title: Nearly 30,000 people visited Hiiumaa's lighthouses last year
World.content:
Estonia currently has 14 lighthouses open to visitors. Three of them are on Hiiumaa island. Last year, Hiiumaa's lighthouses were visited by nearly 30,000 people, accounting for about one‑third of all lighthouse visits in Estonia.

An event marking the reopening of Ristna lighthouse brought great joy to everyone.

"As of today, 14 lighthouses are open. Considering that Estonia has a total of 55 lighthouses, the percentage of open ones is quite good," said Andres Unn, state property manager at the Transport Administration, adding that historical sources claim the metal structure of Ristna lighthouse came from Gustave Eiffel's factory in France.

Hiiumaa is rich in open lighthouses, with three on the island: Ristna, Tahkuna and Kõpu. Locals know that Kõpu lighthouse is unique in the world.

Kõpu lighthouse. Source: ERR

"The idea for Hiiumaa's lighthouse year began with the fact that Kõpu lighthouse turns 495 this year. Among continuously operating lighthouses whose work has never been interrupted — there are two others, not in Estonia — Kõpu is, as far as I know, the oldest," said Kristel Peikel, head of the Hiiumaa tourism cluster.

Tens of thousands of people each year want to climb the stairs to the top of Kõpu lighthouse.

"Ninety‑five percent of people go up the tower, and of those, I think 95 percent also come to the café for at least a coffee if nothing else," said Kõpu lighthouse operator Ene Reidma.

The newly reopened Ristna lighthouse received a fresher look and improved systems thanks to everyone who has spent a few euros in Hiiumaa to enjoy these unique views.

"This latest reconstruction cost 160,000 euros," said Unn.

"A big thank‑you to lighthouse visitors! This is ticket revenue redirected back here to keep the towers in good condition. Hiiumaa municipality also plans to move forward with our major landmark, Kõpu lighthouse," said Antti Leigri, deputy chairman of Hiiumaa municipal council.

The Ristna Lighthouse on Hiiumaa (Dago being the old Baltic German name for the island) before World War One. Source: Indrek Laos.

World.title: Estonia's Robert Virves continues to top WRC2 table after winning in Finland
World.content:
Virves remains top of the second-tier WRC2 table with four races to go, and the win in Finland followed victory before a home crowd at Rally Estonia last month.

Post-race Virves said this was: "A very strange feeling. I don't know what to say. A very long weekend. A lot of drama for everyone. We had a lot of difficulties, others had problems. I'm very happy to be here after all of that. Since it ended this way, I have to accept it."

The Estonian in the Toksport Škoda Fabia was in fact beaten by over 21 seconds in the Rally2 category by local competitor Jari-Matti Latvala, but since the latter was not competing for WRC2 points in the race, Virves seized this opportunity with both hands.

The four wins also mean Virves, 26, has amassed the maximum possible 100 points from the four rallies that have counted towards the standings.

He and co-driver Jakko Viilo went into Sunday's stages second in the WRC2 category, but took the lead after Teemu Suninen, another Finn who had been in the lead, was hit with a 30-second time penalty after failing to stop in the required manner after Estonian driver Patrick Enok's Saturday crash triggered an emergency situation.

In another echo of Rally Estonia, Sami Pajari was dominant all weekend at his home race and took a second consecutive win, after taking victory on the roads of South Estonia in July. Norwegian-Swedish competitor Oliver Solberg was second, while overall WRC table topper Elfyn Evans (Wales) was third.

At 24, Pajari is also now the youngest-ever winner of the Finnish round of the World Rally Championship.

World.title: Deputy police chief on migration pressure: No cause for panic in Estonia
World.content:
Estonia is sending another border guard unit to Latvia to help secure the Latvia-Belarus border amid rising illegal migration pressure, while officials warn that similar attempts could potentially shift toward Estonia's own borders.

Estonia is sending a border guard unit to the Latvia-Belarus border again for two months, where illegal migration pressure is currently the highest. According to Veiko Kommusaar, deputy director general of the Police and Border Guard Board responsible for border guard operations, helping neighboring countries is nothing new for Estonia.

"Indeed, our next rotation will head to Latvia on Monday morning," Kommusaar told Vikerraadio.

"Today, the center of the entire migration pressure is on the Latvian route, and in addition to us, colleagues from Finland and Lithuania are also helping their Latvian counterparts. This is being done so that we have a strong European Union external border and can keep threats outside. Our forecast is that there is no end in sight to this situation at the moment," Kommusaar said.

Although the main pressure is directed toward Latvia, migrants who have entered countries illegally have also reached Estonia. Over the past two weeks, 81 people who arrived illegally via Belarus have been detained in Estonia, with most of them originating from African countries, the PPA deputy chief said.

"They are being organized from here through intermediaries to continue on to other countries," Kommusaar explained. "This week, the aim is to hand over the first detainees to Latvia. The reason is quite simple: while we are helping our Latvian colleagues at the external border as much as we can, they already have established channels for returning these people to the places where they began their journeys."

In addition to dealing with people who have crossed the border illegally, the Police and Border Guard Board is also actively working to catch human traffickers.

"We are focusing very strongly on apprehending intermediaries who earn organized criminal profits from these people's routes of movement — for example, three such people were taken into custody last week," Kommusaar said.

"Why is our route currently standing out and why are alternative routes being sought from here? The reason is that over the years, additional border control and compensatory measures have been introduced between European Union member states and the net has become tighter. This tight net should actually be applied along the entire EU external border so that we can continue to move safely and securely within the Schengen area," the official said.

No cause for concern

Following an incident in Nõmme, where residents noticed a group of unfamiliar people in an apartment building, questions have been raised about public feelings of safety. Kommusaar stressed that there is no reason for concern, but authorities are grateful for any information provided by residents.

"There is certainly no reason for panic today and we are very grateful to people who report suspicious movements to us," he said. "Moving around in groups of dozens of people is not normal and rather indicates that these individuals may not have all their documents in order. They have arrived here via routes that are not legal. Residents certainly do not need to panic because of individual people," Kommusaar said.

Asked whether migration pressure could at some point be directed straight toward the Estonian-Russian border, Kommusaar said this was a real threat.

"A few years ago, similar attempts to cross the border were also made at our border crossing points, as happened in Finland. There have been no such attempts since then, but the threat is real and does exist," Kommusaar noted.

"We know they have both technical support capabilities and a sufficient number of people to organize similar operations in the future either on our borders or on those of our northern neighbors. At the moment, we believe this is unlikely to happen in the near future. However, situations can change quite quickly — if large numbers of people can no longer cross from one area, organizers will undoubtedly look for alternative options. To date, such situations have been supported by Belarus and previously also by our eastern neighbor Russia and they are certainly not ruled out for us and could very likely occur," Kommusaar explained.

World.title: Iraq, Iran discuss developments in the Strait of Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein and his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Aragchi, discussed on Sunday the latest developments in the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for regional de-escalation.

In a phone conversation, the two sides evaluated the most recent developments in the Strait of Hormuz during the last two days, as well as the implications for maritime security and regional stability, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Foreign Ministry.

Hussein emphasized Iraq’s support of dialogue and diplomacy as effective approaches to address disagreements and settle unresolved concerns, thereby helping to improve security and stability in the region.

The discussion also addressed the recent military assaults targeting Iraq and the significance of avoiding any actions that may escalate tensions in the region.

Aragchi reviewed the most recent developments and briefed Hussein on ongoing efforts to reach an agreement that would help reopen the Strait of Hormuz and ensure the smooth flow of maritime navigation.

Iraq is closely monitoring ongoing developments and expects to reach agreements that will facilitate the reopening of the Strait as soon as possible. This effort aims to ensure the security and stability of both the region and the global economy, according to Hussein.

Given the rapidly changing situation, Hussein emphasized the necessity of ongoing coordination between the two parties, as well as his support for steps taken to enhance dialogue.

World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: Iraq, NATO agree to open mission office in Baghdad, expand security cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews,com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi and the commander of the NATO Mission Iraq (NMI), Lt. Gen. Ramon Armada, agreed on Sunday to open a NATO mission office in Baghdad while reaffirming continued cooperation on military training, cybersecurity, and strategic security partnerships.

According to a statement from al-Aboudi’s media office, cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the two officials held talks via video conference to discuss regional security developments and NATO’s ongoing support for Iraq’s armed forces.

During the discussion, both sides stressed the importance of reducing regional tensions and resolving recurring crises through dialogue and diplomatic channels. They also reviewed mechanisms for continuing NATO assistance in the areas of military training, advisory support, intelligence sharing, and capacity building.

A key outcome of the meeting was an agreement to establish a NATO Mission office in Baghdad, further strengthening coordination between the alliance and Iraqi security institutions.

Al-Aboudi said NATO’s role in Iraq remains focused on non-combat activities, including military advisory services, training, capacity building, cybersecurity support, and cooperation in artificial intelligence. He added that Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government is pursuing a policy of engagement with friendly and neighboring countries to advance development, investment, and mutually beneficial partnerships.

For his part, Armada reaffirmed that NATO’s advisory and training mission is committed to helping develop the capabilities of Iraq’s armed forces to address future security challenges. He said the alliance remains committed to supporting Iraq in line with the priorities established by the Iraqi government.

World.title: Zaidi threatens to resign as Coordination Framework divided over response to Saudi strikes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly threatened to resign during a recent meeting of the Coordination Framework amid deep divisions over how Iraq should respond to recent Saudi military strikes, according to a report published Sunday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada.

Citing political sources, the newspaper said the prime minister’s remarks came during a tense meeting that exposed growing disagreements among senior Shiite leaders over security policy, the role of armed factions, and Baghdad’s handling of escalating regional tensions.

According to the report, the meeting became increasingly heated after intelligence was presented alleging that the armed group Saraya Awliya al-Dam was preparing to launch an attack against Jordan from Iraqi territory. The sources said Amman had warned Baghdad it would respond to any attack originating from Iraq, further intensifying the debate.

The report claims the dispute centered on whether Iraq should adhere to the government’s official position or allow individual armed factions to respond independently to the recent Saudi strikes. While most Coordination Framework leaders reportedly backed the government’s approach, one influential figure with ties to Saraya Awliya al-Dam insisted on carrying out a unilateral response.

Al-Mada reported that armed factions have given the government until next Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia. According to the sources, they warned that if Baghdad fails to act, they may launch their own response.

The newspaper also reported that the escalating dispute prompted al-Zaidi to again raise the possibility of resigning, marking what would be the second time he has reportedly made such a threat since taking office. According to the report, he previously suggested stepping down if his anti-corruption agenda failed.

The sources further claimed that the prime minister is facing mounting political pressure, including concerns about his personal security, although no official statements have confirmed those assertions.

The report also focused on the investigation into drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, stating that seven Iraqi-Saudi security meetings, with U.S. participation in some sessions, have been held over the past two months.

According to Al-Mada’s sources, the investigations have not produced conclusive evidence proving that the attacks originated from Iraqi territory, despite Saudi accusations.

The report said several scenarios remain under discussion, including the possibility that Iraqi armed factions were responsible, that Houthi operatives present in Iraq facilitated the attacks, or alternative theories promoted by some factions alleging Israeli activity in Iraq’s southern desert regions.

According to the newspaper, the ongoing crisis led al-Zaidi to cancel a planned visit to Saudi Arabia, which Iraqi officials reportedly viewed as an opportunity to attract much-needed Saudi investment at a time when Iraq faces mounting financial pressures.

The report also said armed factions have urged the prime minister to suspend efforts to bring all weapons under state control, arguing that the recent Saudi strikes have fundamentally altered the security landscape.

Al-Mada also reported that discussions during the meeting touched on the role of Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Faleh al-Fayyadh during the recent U.S.-Saudi strikes that targeted PMF facilities.

According to the newspaper’s sources, claims circulated that al-Zaidi had warned al-Fayyadh upon returning from Turkey that PMF sites could be targeted, and that evacuation efforts were delayed. However, other participants reportedly dismissed those claims, suggesting they reflected internal political disputes rather than established facts.

The Iraqi government has previously denied having prior knowledge of the U.S.-Saudi strikes. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad neither approved nor was informed in advance of the attacks.

However, U.S. President Donald Trump later told Fox News that the strikes had been coordinated with the Iraqi government, presenting an account that differs from Baghdad’s official position.

World.title: Zaidi’s failed raid on Nujaba base exposes challenges in disarmament push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A failed security operation targeting a facility belonging to the Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba movement has underscored the challenges facing the Iraqi government as it seeks to bring all armed groups under state control before the end of September.

According to a report published by Al-Monitor, a joint Iraqi force attempted to search a Harakat al-Nujaba compound in Baghdad’s Jurf al-Naddaf district on July 24 after receiving intelligence suggesting the site contained missiles and drones. However, the operation ended without the facility being searched after armed members of the group confronted government forces.

The report, citing Iraqi security officials, said the operation involved Baghdad Operations Command, the Federal Police, and the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Security Directorate. Shortly after arriving at the compound, commanders affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba reportedly ordered their fighters to prevent security personnel from entering. Armed members of the group then surrounded the government force and fired warning shots into the air, forcing the operation to halt.

According to the officials, the PMF leadership subsequently instructed its personnel to withdraw, stating they had not been informed that the target was a facility affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba. Army units involved in the operation later received similar withdrawal orders. No casualties were reported, and neither the government nor the armed group publicly disclosed details of the incident at the time.

The incident comes as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that all weapons in Iraq are brought under state control by September 30, the scheduled end of the U.S.-led coalition’s military mission in the country.

Al-Monitor described the failed operation as the first significant field test of the government’s commitment to enforcing that pledge. While previous administrations also announced plans to limit weapons to state institutions, implementation has remained difficult due to the political and military influence of several armed factions.

Hayder al-Shakeri, a researcher with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, told Al-Monitor that although Baghdad has increasingly relied on restructuring security institutions and applying political and financial pressure on armed groups, the Jurf al-Naddaf operation demonstrated the limits of the state’s authority when confronted directly.

“If the government cannot enforce its decisions against a single armed faction, or fails to follow through with legal and political accountability, it suggests that these groups still retain an effective veto over certain state actions,” Al-Shakeri was quoted as saying.

The report noted that not all Iran-aligned factions share the same position regarding government efforts to centralize weapons under state control.

Some groups, including Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have become increasingly integrated into Iraq’s political and economic systems, potentially reducing their willingness to engage in direct confrontation. Others—including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada—continue to oppose any move that would place their military capabilities under full government authority.

Political analyst Muhannad al-Ghazi told Al-Monitor that these factions view their weapons through an ideological lens, making voluntary disarmament highly unlikely. He argued that targeting isolated weapons caches without addressing broader military infrastructure would have only a limited impact.

The reported confrontation occurred amid heightened regional tensions following Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington, where Iraq and the United States announced a strategic economic partnership.

According to Al-Monitor, several Iran-backed factions criticized the visit, warning against what they described as replacing “military occupation” with “economic occupation” through expanded U.S. investment in Iraq.

The report also linked the incident to broader regional developments, including recent drone attacks and cross-border military operations that have intensified pressure on Baghdad’s efforts to assert control over its territory.

Al-Monitor concluded that the government’s September 30 target for fully disarming armed factions appears increasingly difficult to achieve given current realities.

Instead, analysts cited by the publication believe Baghdad may focus on more gradual measures, including relocating some weapons, closing selected facilities, and increasing political and financial pressure on groups willing to cooperate, while avoiding direct confrontation with the most heavily armed factions.

The report suggested that the ultimate success of Iraq’s disarmament strategy may depend not only on domestic enforcement but also on broader regional dynamics, particularly relations between the United States and Iran.

Abhijeet Dipke says he's ready to reveal degree after RTI over foreign fundings (Image/PTI)

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday challenged BJP leaders to make their educational qualifications public after an RTI query was filed seeking details of the funding for his studies abroad.In a video message shared on social media, Dipke said he was ready to disclose all documents related to his education."I just saw that a BJP worker has filed an RTI against me. World.title: Lok Sabha clears bill to increase number of Supreme Court judges, without debate
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Monday passed the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges from the present 33 to 37 (excluding the Chief Justice of India).

The bill, which will now be sent to the Rajya Sabha for consideration, was passed without a debate as opposition members continued raising slogans over the NEET paper leak and the alleged theft of donations from the Ram temple.

After a brief introductory statement by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal, the Chair invited MPs to speak. However, with the sloganeering continuing, the bill was put to a voice vote and passed.

Following the passage of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, the House was adjourned for the day.

On May 5, the Union Cabinet approved the introduction of the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 in Parliament. The legislation seeks to amend the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956, which provides for an increase in the number of Supreme Court judges, excluding the Chief Justice.

World.title: Needs 'decoding': RSS leader Atul Limaye links CJP protest to 'subversion of democracy', Dipke hits back
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

(RSS) leader Atul Limaye has alleged that the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest over the NEET-UG paper leak evolved into an "experiment for alternative politics", claiming that several political, student, labour and civil society organisations joined the agitation to propagate the idea of "subversion of democracy through democratic means.

"

Addressing an ABVP event in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar on July 30, Limaye said the protest should be "decoded" to understand its chronology, methodology, support system and ideological underpinnings. He also alleged that anti-Hindu and "anti-national" slogans were raised during the agitation and questioned how it transformed from a student-led protest into a broader political movement.

During his address, Limaye said, "In Today's times, CJP agitation should be studied as a case study.

This has now come to the knowledge of everyone, but this was A phenomenon going on for years now. And if we have to study this whole agitation, we will have to see its full chronology, methodology and what their support system is, and the innovative system which they used and the ideology behind it. Of we see chronology, Abhijit Dipke was from our Marathwada itself.

When he launched CJP, he got tremendous following (on social Media), and when he came back to India, he came back on 6th June and did his agitation on 7th."





Describing the course of the agitation, he added, "But he didn't receive the response which was expected. So, he roamed around the country from 7th to 19th. He started agitation in various cities of the country, or tried to start agitation, but even there did not get that kind of response. So, he started agitation, sit-in protest at Jantar Mantar from the 20th onwards, and gradually the face of the agitation got changed.

"

According to Limaye, the movement later drew the participation of student organisations, labour unions, human rights groups, women's organisations, farmers' bodies and other civil society groups.

He said, "What kind of things happened after that which changed the face of this agitation? What kind of support system did attach to this agitation? We need to see which organisations and institutions got attached to this agitation, and this will give us an idea of what kind of support system.

This agitation obviously involved the youth, the students of the country. And that is why several student organisations got attached to it.

Among the prominent organisations which were leading the stage in this protest was All India Student Association (AISA). And the second such Association was SFI."

He further said, "Some human rights organisations, many tribal organisations, women organisations like Pinjra Tod joined them.

Many Muslim organisations, Christian organisations, some institutions working in the legal sector, environment sector, journalistic associations also joined them. Some farmers' associations joined them, as Samyukta Kisan Morcha and Bharatiya Kisan Union joined them."

Invoking Italian philosopher Antonio Gramsci's theory of cultural hegemony, Limaye argued that the protest was aimed at challenging democratic institutions and cultural values while operating within democratic processes.

He said, "Why did the opposition to Hindus arise from the stage? Why were leaders from several political parties seen on the stage, and how did it convert from a student protest to a political protest? It was not limited to Delhi, but expanded in all the states. For this, we have to decode Yogendra Yadav's remark, 'Democracy's future now will not be decided in Parliament but on streets, elections will not decide, resistance will.

' The cause of the protest was genuine, but who captured the movement? If we understand this, then we will understand this protest. There is a lot to learn. This protest was an experiment for an alternative politics."

He added, "This theory states subversion of democracy through democratic means. This is well documented, and Italian scholar Gramsci gave the theory of cultural hegemony. He said that cultural hegemony needs to be destroyed for revolution.

The deconstruction theory challenged Lord Ram and other figures. Alternative politics states that till there is a system, like our Parliamentary system, there cannot be revolution.

All the systems, including the judiciary and police, need to be challenged."

Claiming that such politics could be pursued either electorally or through weakening public faith in institutions, Limaye said, "There are two ways: one is election and the second is subversion of democracy through democratic means.

There is infiltration in the judiciary, education system, and bureaucracy. Second is challenging the institutions and eroding faith in them. The results are so dangerous. Many police officers said the way the women were behaving, it was difficult to tolerate.

The way they were dressed and the language they used, we were ashamed. This was an attempt to degrade the culture."

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke rejected the allegations and said the RSS had no moral authority to describe others as anti-national.

Responding to Limaye's remarks on Monday, Dipke referred to the period when the RSS was banned following Mahatma Gandhi's assassination.

Abhijeet Dipke said, "People who murdered Mahatma Gandhi are calling us anti-national. The murderers of Mahatma Gandhi have no moral right to call anyone else anti-national. Nathuram Godse was the first anti-national."

The CJP had led a 37-day protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG paper leak. The agitation was withdrawn on July 25 after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the organisation said it had received assurances on its other key demands.

World.title: 'Neither officer using excessive force, nor criminal protester should be protected': SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday observed that "neither a police officer using excessive force nor a hardened criminal under the garb of a student protest should be protected.

" These remarks came as it heard petitions related to the NEET-UG protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20.

The apex court said states are free to close or withdraw FIRs registered against student protesters, provided it is done in accordance with law. The court also indicated that it may lay down guidelines on the use of pellet guns during protests.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the term "criminal antecedents" refers only to grave and heinous offences, addressing concerns that students booked in minor or political cases could be denied relief.

During the hearing, the CJI stressed that the court wanted to strike a balance between protecting peaceful protesters and ensuring accountability for serious offenders.

"A police officer involved in excessive force should not be unduly protected. And it should not be that a hardened criminal under the garb of student protest is also getting protected," the CJI observed.

On allegations that pellet guns were used during the protest, the CJI said the court was considering issuing guidelines.





"We would like to lay down a protocol on how it can be used," he said.

The bench noted that petitions had been filed both by protesters alleging excessive police force and by police personnel claiming they were injured during the violence.

Appearing for the Centre, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the court that the Union government remained committed to its assurance that cases against student protesters would not be pursued, except in cases involving serious criminal offences.

He said FIRs against more than 2,700 people with antecedents involving grave and heinous offences would not be withdrawn, according to ANI.

Mehta also said there had been a misunderstanding regarding the government's stand on the issue. "Barring those with criminal antecedents, the government is prepared to address the cases against the student protesters. Let them sit with the government. There are some people who want to keep the pot boiling so we have to be cautious about the legal advice," he said.

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing for some petitioners, urged the court to examine allegations of police excesses during the protest. He said the petitioners had submitted around 300 videos showing the alleged use of force.

"The videos are very shocking. We have given 300 videos to the court. Since directions have come from the top, the commissioner of police must look at all this," he said.

He further submitted, "Ideally, we have identified un-uniformed individuals committing such police excess.

A direction has to go to the Commissioner of Police and the RAF Director as to why police used pellet guns etc."

Senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi sought clarification on the expression "criminal antecedents", arguing that it should not include minor offences.

"These are students, somebody may have a driving violation or a petty offence, or due to a political case. The word criminal antecedent needs to be clarified," Singhvi said, according to Live Law.

He urged the court to exclude petty offences and cases arising out of political protests from the definition. Last week, the apex court had indicated that it would constitute a Special Investigation Team (SIT) to investigate the July 20 incident and directed authorities to preserve CCTV footage and other official records related to the protest.

The hearing comes days after the Supreme Court declined an oral plea seeking suo motu cognisance of the police action during the 'Chalo Sansad' protest.

The court had earlier observed that police excesses or a lathi charge could not be justified merely because an agitation was taking place and underlined that the right to peaceful protest is "absolutely guaranteed."

World.title: Congress workers detained while protesting E20 fuel outside Gadkari's residence: Watch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Police on Monday detained Congress workers protesting against the Centre's ethanol-blended fuel policy outside Union Minister Nitin Gadkari's residence in Nagpur.

"We condemn E20 being imposed on us. We will continue to fight," said youth congress leader Mehul Adwani.

The protest march began at Chitnavis Park Square in Mahal and proceeded towards Gadkari's private residence in the same locality, with Youth Congress workers raising slogans against the use of E20 ethanol-blended fuel, calling it unviable.

A heavy police presence was deployed near the Union minister's residence, with barricades erected along the route.

Some protesters attempted to climb over the barricades to continue the march before being stopped by the police.

The Congress has been targeting Gadkari over the nationwide rollout of E20 fuel, arguing that his statement in Parliament on July 29 raised more questions than it answered.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh on Monday said Gadkari had maintained that E20 petrol was introduced after years of scientific testing and that there was no evidence of widespread damage to vehicles caused by the fuel.





"For months now, consumers and mechanics across the country have been reporting: reduced mileage; engine performance issues; concerns over the long-term impact of E20 fuel on their vehicles; engine compatibility, cold-start problems, and accelerated wear and tear in pre-2023 vehicles; increasing instances of clogged injectors, corroded fuel lines and cracked rubber components in older vehicles," Ramesh said in a post on X.

AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Monday said he would lead a march to prime minister Narendra Modi's residence on Tuesday with 100 people to submit petitions opposing E20 fuel. He alleged that the Centre was promoting ethanol-blended fuel under pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Kejriwal further claimed that India had "yielded" to Trump by agreeing to import ethanol from the United States and alleged that the government's continued push for E20 petrol pointed to a "hidden agenda".

World.title: 'Do not befriend Kaafirs': Pakistani general levels terror allegations against India
World.content:
Pakistan's military spokesperson Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry

Pakistan's military spokesperson, Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, has sparked controversy after saying in a video that Muslims should not befriend "kaafirs" (non-believers), warning that those who do would no longer be considered among the faithful."Do not befriend kaafirs (non-believers) and leave the faithful. If you do that, there's a problem. Then you are not among the Muslims," Chaudhry said while addressing a press conference.âNow our population is 240-250 million people, and we still have four provinces. We have to see whether this is serving the purpose of good governance. That debate has to be sensibly held by politicians, by those in power, even those who have previously been in power, and those who are responsible to the people of Pakistan,â he added.The remarks were made during a wider media briefing that focused on Pakistan's counter-terrorism operations, the security situation in Balochistan, and the country's ties with Afghanistan.Taking a jibe at India-Afghanistan ties, Chaudhry claimed that the Afghan Taliban regime's "business" was terrorism, alleging that it used militancy to sustain its economy, state institutions and diplomacy.âEven their diplomacy is centred on terrorism. What is common between India and Afghanistan, except their DNA? The only thing common is terrorism,â Chaudhary said, as cited by Dawn.Chaudhry also claimed that around 300 Indian websites were being used to support terrorism-related activities in Balochistan, while more than 1,000 social media accounts and what he described as a "hostile diaspora" were involved in spreading propaganda linked to terrorism.âFirst, an event or incident is seeded, right or wrong, and then it is framed by initiators, who hand it over to amplifiers. Then mass amplification is done by mainstream Indian media, channels and their print media as well, from where it is picked up by international media, and then you take it and run it as facts," he said.The DG ISPR said the government was also working to strengthen the police force, including by deploying newly recruited assistant superintendents of police (ASPs) to Balochistan and providing bulletproof vehicles, among other measures.The remarks come amid a series of attacks on Pakistani security forces across Balochistan last month, with armed clashes also reported during military operations in the Mastung and Kech districts, according to The Balochistan Post (TBP).The insurgency in Balochistan has been led by several separatist groups, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), which has waged a long-running campaign against Pakistan's federal government. The group has frequently targeted security personnel and infrastructure in the province and has also carried out attacks in other parts of the country, including Karachi.According to Pakistan's 2023 census, Balochistan is home to around 15 million people and is rich in natural resources, including coal, gold, copper and natural gas. The BLA maintains that these resources should belong to the people of Balochistan and opposes the federal government's control over their extraction and the province's security.

World.title: Kerala rain fury: 15 dead, 7 missing as relief camps shelter thousands
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Chief minister VD Satheesan on Monday said that the death toll in rain-related incidents across Kerala has risen to 15 as heavy rainfall continued to batter the state and rescue operations intensified.

Addressing a press conference after reviewing the flood situation with senior officials, Satheesan said 316 relief camps were functioning across Kerala, sheltering 11,018 people displaced by flooding and landslides.

He said Kottayam reported three deaths, including two in the Poonjar assembly constituency and a child who drowned after falling into a water tank. Ernakulam recorded two deaths, while one person each died in Idukki and Muvattupuzha.

Four people died in Malappuram, two in Kollam and one each in Kannur and Kozhikode.

The chief minister said seven people were still missing. Two each are missing in Kollam and Kannur, while one person each is untraceable in Malappuram, Idukki and Muvattupuzha.

Satheesan announced Rs 10,000 as funeral assistance for the families of those killed in rain-related incidents. He also said people returning home from flooded relief camps would receive Rs 10,000 as immediate assistance.





The chief minister directed the Agriculture Department to submit a proposal to revise crop compensation, saying the current relief was inadequate. According to preliminary estimates, 165 hectares of agricultural land have been damaged, affecting 3,596 farmers.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued rain alerts for all 14 districts in the state. Orange alerts are in place for Kasaragod, Kannur, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Malappuram, Ernakulam, Idukki, Kottayam, Alappuzha and Pathanamthitta, while Palakkad, Thrissur, Kollam and Thiruvananthapuram remain under a yellow alert.

The weather office has forecast isolated heavy rainfall accompanied by gusty winds of up to 60 kmph.

Authorities have urged people living in low-lying and riverside areas to remain alert as water levels in major rivers continue to rise. Residents in landslide-prone hilly regions have also been advised to move to safer locations if necessary.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

District collectors have declared a holiday for educational institutions in 12 districts, including professional colleges, due to the heavy rain.

The ban on fishing along the Kerala, Karnataka and Lakshadweep coasts also remains in force because of rough sea conditions.

In Pathanamthitta district, rising water levels in the Pamba river have raised concerns after recent flash floods. Authorities have warned that the Moozhiyar Dam may be opened if water levels continue to rise and have asked residents along the riverbanks to stay prepared for evacuation.

The Kerala government said it remains fully prepared to handle any emergency and urged people to strictly follow advisories issued by the state and district administrations. It also said financial assistance would be provided to families of those killed and to people who lost their homes and livelihoods.

World.title: Coastal erosion washed away road, threatens hundreds of homes in Kasaragod
World.content:
Severe sea erosion triggered by rough monsoon conditions has washed away the Cherangai-Kavungoli coastal road at Kavugoli in Mogral Puthur, leaving around 200 families cut off and without road access. The sea has advanced nearly 100 metres inland at Kavugoli, completely destroying the coastal road. Residents fear strong waves could inundate their homes at any moment as the erosion continues unabated.

Apart from Kavugoli, severe coastal erosion has been reported from Nellikunnu, Cherangai, Uduma, Pallikkara, and Musodi in Uppala. At Musodi, a house is on the verge of being swallowed by the sea. Protection measures, including geobags installed along vulnerable stretches, have been severely damaged or washed away. Several houses remain under threat while families living in the high-risk areas have already been shifted to safer locations.

At Koyippady beach in Kumbla, large sections of the stone seawall have been eroded, with the remaining geobag protection is also being washed away. Residents fear that if the adjoining coastal road collapses, hundreds of nearby houses will be at risk.

At Pervard beach, the geobag seawall installed two years ago has been completely destroyed, while the remaining stone seawall is also being eroded. Residents allege that all seawalls constructed along the beach over the past decades have failed over the years, accusing authorities of spending crores of rupees on ineffective coastal protection works.

Institute at risk

Sea erosion has also intensified along other coastal stretches, including CPCRI, Thrikkannad, Valiyaparamba, Chembarikka, and Ajanur. The erosion has also severely affected the beach experimental block of the ICAR- Central Plantation Crops Research Institute. The institute, which has nearly 1 km of boundary along the Arabian Sea, has lost approximately 80 metres of its compound wall to erosion. Another 30 metres of the wall remains in a precarious condition, raising concerns about further damage if the erosion continues.

According to the institute, around 30 metres of land that once separated its boundary from the sea has been completely washed away due to repeated high tides and and continuous erosion bringing the sea dangerously close to its experimental farm. Officials warned that further erosion could cause extensive damage to the research fields and infrastructure.

The institute has informed the District Collector, local MLA, MP, panchayat president and the Minor Irrigation department seeking immediate intervention to protect the experimental farm. Local residents have demanded scientifically designed and permanent coastal protection measures such as tetrapods or concrete seawalls instead of relying on conventional stone embankments to prevent recurring destruction along Kasaragod’s coastline.

World.title: Supreme Court asks govt to consider ‘important’ plea that Jantar Mantar is not the right site for protests
World.content:
The Supreme Court asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta on Monday (August 3, 2026) to consult with Union Government authorities on an “important” petition that Jantar Mantar is not the “right site” to hold protests.

“The petition says Jantar Mantar is not the right site anymore for such protests due to ingress-egress issue, supply of medical essentials, sewage, etc… I think this is important. I think this is important. Please take instructions, Mr. Solicitor. Issue notice and list this separately,” Chief Justice Surya Kant, heading a three-judge Bench, addressed the top law officer.

The petition filed by Satish Chand Kaushik, represented by advocate Aakarshan Aditya, urged the discontinuation of Jantar Mantar as the ordinary designated venue for public protests and demonstrations, and to designate Ramlila Maidan, or another sufficiently large and secure ground, as the principal protest venue for the national capital.

Mr. Aditya argued that Jantar Mantar was designated in an earlier era for limited, identifiable and manageable demonstrations.

“Today, digitally mobilised movements can transform a few hundred persons into several thousand within hours, without a reliable command structure, verified organisers or an enforceable estimate of attendance. Its proximity to Parliament, Central Vista, government establishments, diplomatic and commercial areas creates an avoidable convergence of mass mobilisation, national-security sensitivity and restricted physical space,” the counsel submitted.

The petitioner said the ordinary people were finding it extremely hard to commute in Central Delhi due to prolonged traffic snarls due to the protests and demonstrations. Mr. Kaushik’s side referred to the Aam Aadmi Party National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal’s national townhall programme held outside the Constitution Club to protest the implementation of the E20 policy.

“Another July 20 incident should be avoided,” the petitioner counsel said.

“They [the government] know how to handle it. If they cannot, come to us,” Chief Justice Kant said.

The petition has come days after the Court’s repeated observations upholding the right of citizens to peaceful and lawful protest. The Court had however balanced the freedom to express dissent with the right to not break the peace or occupy public space.

In 2018, the Supreme Court had held that the golden rule was that the right to protest should be balanced with the right of the residents to live peacefully. The observation had come in a decision lifting the ban on protests at Jantar Mantar and Boat Club.

“Democracy and dissent go hand in hand, but then the demonstrations expressing dissent have to be in designated places alone,” the Court had noted.

In its 2020 judgment in the Shaheen Bagh case, a three-judge Bench had held that fundamental rights did not live in isolation. “The right of the protester has to be balanced with the right of the commuter. They have to co-exist in mutual respect,” the Court had said in a judgment which found the indefinite “occupation” of a public road by the Shaheen Bagh protestors unacceptable.

World.title: Attack on ED officials: Kerala HC grants bail to 9 accused
World.content:
The Kerala High Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) allowed the bail petitions of nine accused in the attack on Enforcement Directorate (ED) officials during the raid on former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan's residence in Thiruvananthapuram in May 2026.

Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail, with conditions, reasoning that the accused have been in remand for more than 60 days and that they had no other criminal history. The court also noted that the offence of attempted murder could not be made out against the accused and that the investigation had reached its final stage.

The raid was conducted by the ED officials on the residences of Mr. Vijayan in Kannur and Thiruvananthapuram. It was connected to the inquiry into Exalogic Solutions, a now-defunct firm, owned by T. Veena, Mr. Vijayan's daughter, on the allegations that the company was receiving monthly payments from Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL), a private mining company.

World.title: Delhi High Court refuses bail to ex-MLA Naresh Balyan in MCOCA case
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) refused to grant bail to former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA Naresh Balyan in a case under the stringent law against organised crime.

"We are dismissing it," Justice Manoj Jain said while pronouncing the verdict on Mr. Balyan's bail plea.

The ex-lawmaker was arrested in the case under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) on December 4, 2024, the same day a trial court granted him bail in an alleged extortion case.

Seeking bail, he had contended that there was "no shred of evidence" against him and the case against him was "completely frivolous".

Mr. Balyan is accused of being a "facilitator" in an organised crime syndicate.

On January 15, 2025, a trial court had denied bail to Mr. Balyan in the case.

The prosecutor had then cited 16 FIRs lodged against the alleged syndicate members in various parts of Delhi, claiming the syndicate had created havoc in society and amassed huge illegal wealth.

World.title: Tamil Nadu moves Supreme Court against Karnataka in Cauvery water row
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu government headed by Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay moved the Supreme Court on Monday (August 3, 2026) for a direction to the State of Karnataka to implement a Central Water Management Authority (CWMA) decision of July 30 to ensure the release of 3,500 cusecs for 15 days from its two reservoirs at Kabini and Krishna Raja Sagara.

Editorial | Distress and dispute: On Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and the Cauvery

Tamil Nadu’s approach to the Supreme Court for the release of 4.536 TMC (at the rate of 3,500 cusecs for 15 days) on or before August 12 has come even as Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the water situation has become “slightly better” while urging Kannada organisations to withdraw their State-wide bandh plan on August 13.

The Tamil Nadu application, finalised by senior advocates C.S. Vaidyanathan and G. Umapathy, and drafted by Tushar Nair, was filed by advocate-on-record B. Karunakaran. The State urged the Court to direct the CWMA to issue an appropriate direction to Karnataka to make good, on a pro-rata basis, the shortfall at the inter-State point of Billigundulu for the period from June 1 to August 12, and in this regard release 26.954 TMC of water forthwith.

It further sought an order to the CWMA to monitor the flows in the reservoirs of Karnataka every 10 days and ensure stipulated monthly/daily releases at Billigundulu.

The Tamil Nadu government said Karnataka had continued to defy the orders of the Cauvery Tribunal for allocation of water to its neighbour except a few times when there were inevitable surpluses in the reservoirs on account of floods.

The State said the had reviewed the hydrometeorological condition in Cauvery basin on July 30 and endorsed the July 28 recommendations of the Cauvery Water Regulations Committee (CWRC) to release waters from Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS) and Kabini reservoir at the rate of 3,500 cusecs from July 29 for 15 days.

Comment | A gamble on the Cauvery issue

“Even if Karnataka ensured flows of 3,500 cusecs for 15 days, it would get only 4.536 TMC leaving a backlog of 5.379 TMC even as per the pro rata assessment of distress as on July 28... 28.07.2026. If the inflows into the 4 major reservoirs of Karnataka against 30 years average up to August 3, 2026 is considered, the pro-rata ratio works out to 46.34%. Based on this pro-rata ratio, the flows due from June 1, 2026 to August 12, 2026 works out to 26.95 TMC. The direction given by the CWRC and CWMA is only 4.536 TMC, which is far less than the quantum of water as per distress proportion,” the Tamil Nadu application said.

The State argued that despite the CWRC/CWMA interventions, total flows realised at Billigundulu from July 29 to August 2 were only in the range of 158 cusecs to 530 cusecs.

“Thus, it is evident that Karnataka has willfully not complied with the directions of CWRC/CWMA. It is stated that as on August 3, Karnataka is having 23.078 TMC in KRS, 18.610 TMC in Kabini, 7.827 TMC in Harangi and 28.022 TMC in Hemavathy, totally 77.537 TMC of gross storage... This increase in the live storage is on account of recent heavy rainfall in the catchments upstream of Kabini and KRS. Thus, Karnataka in spite of having adequate storage has failed to comply with the directions of CWMA,” Tamil Nadu contended.

During the current irrigation year of 2026-2027, Tamil Nadu said the catchments upstream of KRS, Kabini and the uncontrolled catchment during the period from June 1 to July 27 received a total rainfall of 488.0 mm, 676.1 mm, and 78.4 mm, respectively, against the normal rainfall of 633.4 mm, 1160.2 mm and 119.5 mm, respectively.

“The rainfall deficit in the catchment upstream of KRS, Kabini and in the uncontrolled catchment was 23%, 42% and 34%, respectively,” the application said.

Tamil Nadu said the monthly stipulated flows to be ensured by Karnataka during June to September at Billigundulu were 123.14 TMC, and from October to January was 44.11 TMC, comprising a total of 167.25 TMC every year. In addition, 10 TMC was allocated for meeting the environmental flows during every year making a total of 177.25 TMC.

World.title: Cyberabad Police advise staggered early office departures on August 3 amid heavy rain forecast
World.content:
The Cyberabad Traffic Police on Monday (August 3, 2026) issued a traffic advisory requesting companies and organisations across the commissionerate to allow employees to leave office early in a staggered manner following forecasts of moderate to heavy rainfall.

The advisory, issued by the Office of the Joint Commissioner of Police (Traffic), urged employers to begin staggered logouts from 3.30 p.m. on August 3 to reduce travel-related risks, ease pressure on the road network and ensure the smooth movement of emergency services.

The police said the measure was recommended in view of an official weather alert predicting adverse conditions that could lead to severe traffic congestion across Cyberabad. The Traffic Police appealed to companies and organisations to cooperate in the interest of public safety and to minimise disruptions caused by the expected rain.

Officials said staggering employee departures would help prevent a surge in traffic during peak hours, reduce the likelihood of bottlenecks on major roads and allow emergency vehicles to move without obstruction.

The Cyberabad Traffic Police thanked organisations for their understanding and cooperation, stating that coordinated efforts would help ensure safer travel and the uninterrupted functioning of essential services during the inclement weather.

World.title: Kerala rains LIVE | Death toll reaches 15, seven remain missing, says CM V.D. Satheesan
World.content:
The death toll in rain-related incidents across Kerala has risen to 15, while seven people remain missing, Chief Minister V D Satheesan said on Monday (August 3, 2026), as the State intensified rescue and relief operations amid continuing heavy rain.

As of 9 am, as many as 316 relief camps were functioning across the State, sheltering 11,018 people displaced by the rain and flooding, the Chief Minister told a press conference after reviewing the flood situation with top officials.

Although the intensity of the rain has subsided, moderate heavy rain continues to affect the State. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) upgraded the rain alert for Kerala from yellow to orange on Monday, warning of intense heavy rainfall. As of 1 pm, 12 districts are on orange alert.

World.title: One dead, two missing so far as heavy rain continues to batter Kerala’s Kannur
World.content:
Heavy monsoon rains continued to batter Kannur district of Kerala, leaving one person dead, two injured and two others missing so far, while 521 people have been shifted to eight relief camps as on Monday.

The rains have affected 32 villages, with flooding reported in 13 villages. Authorities have recorded five landslips, while no major landslides have been reported. The district has reported damage to 60 houses, including two that were completely destroyed and 58 that were partially damaged.

Pazhassi spillway shutters opened

Meanwhile, the Pazhassi barrage continued to discharge large volumes of water. At 8 a.m, the barrage recorded an inflow of 1,288.605 cubic metres per second and an outflow of 1,14.132 cumecs through the spillway. Water storage stood at 1.666 million cubic metres, with the water level at 16.75 metres. The catchment received 40.22 mm of rainfall during the 24 hours ending at 7 a.m.

Of the barrage’s 16 spillway shutters, 15 were open – most by 5 metres and three by 4.5 metres – while one shutter remained closed. All three Left Bank Canal (LBC) shutters remained fully closed.

Authorities have urged people living along riverbanks and low-lying areas to remain vigilant as heavy inflows continue into the reservoir.

World.title: PM Shehbaz congratulates PML-N after party maintains lead in second phase of AJK polls
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates on Monday after unofficial results of the second phase of elections in Azad Jammu and Kashmir showed it had won 14 of 18 seats up for grabs the previous day.

The PML-N’s main rival in the contest and also its ally in the Centre, the PPP, has accused the PML-N of electoral malpractices, rigging and violence during Sunday polls, as it had during the first phase of the elections in Mirpur division on July 27. The PML-N secured nine of the 13 seats in the first phase while the PPP won the remaining four.

Elections in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with polling having been held on seven seats of Muzaffarabad division and 12 refugee seats — the reserved seats for refugees from India-occupied Kashmir — on Sunday. In the third phase, elections will be held in 11 constituencies of Poonch division.

‘Results reflect people’s confidence in PML-N’s policies’

A statement released by the PM’s Office on Monday said the premier congratulated PML-N’s leadership and successful candidates after their win in the second phase.

“The continuity of this success is a result of the hard work of PML-N President Nawaz Sharif and the entire PML-N team,” the statement quoted PM Shehbaz as saying

According to the statement, the premier noted that Nawaz and the PML-N team had conducted a successful electoral campaign in AJK and the party’s success “reflects the confidence of the people of AJK in PML-N’s policies”.

He said the development and prosperity of AJK and the welfare of its people remained PML-N’s top priority.

PM Shehbaz added that political parties had actively participated in the second phase of the AJK elections, which he said would further strengthen the democratic process.

Results breakdown

Earlier, state broadcaster Radio Pakistan reported the unofficial results of Sunday’s elections, citing Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal’s press talk in Muzaffarabad.

During the press briefing, he announced that the PML-N had won 14 seats and the PPP four, the report said.

Unofficial results

LA-34 bagged by PML-N’s Nasir Dar

LA-35 bagged by PML-N’s Chaudhry Muhammad Ismail

LA-36 bagged by PML-N’s Muhammad Ahsan Raza

LA-37 bagged by PNL-N’s Maryam Javed

LA-38 bagged by PML-N’s Zeeshah Ali

LA-39 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Muhammad Siddique Khan

LA-41 bagged by PML-N’s Muhammad Amir Shah

LA-42 bagged by PML-N’s Syed Shawkat Ali Shah

LA-43 bagged by PML-N’s Muhammad Yasin Lone

LA-44 bagged by PML-N’s Ahmad Raza Qadiri

LA-25 bagged by PML-N’s Ghulam Qadir

LA-30 bagged by PML-N’s Mustafa Bashir Abbasi

LA-31 bagged by PML-N’s Saqib Majeed Khan

LA-32 bagged by PML-N’s Raja Farooq Haider Khan

LA-40 bagged by PPP’s Amir Abdul Ghaffar Khan

LA-45 bagged by PPP’s Abdul Majid Khan

LA-26 bagged by PPP’s Mian Abdul Waheed Khan

LA-29 bagged by PPP’s Sardar Mukhtar Ahmad Khan

Polling was postponed until Tuesday in LA-27 Muzaffarabad-I (Kutla) and at 71 of the 174 polling stations in LA-28 Muzaffarabad-II (Lachhrat) as polling staff and election material could not reach the constituency because of landslides and bad weather that resulted in blocked roads.

PML-N now has ‘simple majority’ to form govt: Rana Sana

As the unofficial results were released, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs and PML-N leader Rana Sanaullah said his party had now gained the “simple majority” needed to form a government in AJK.

He was addressing a press conference alongside Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam.

“We have the government-forming number,” he said, adding that “there are a total of 45 seats […] and out of 45, PML-N has so far secured 23 seats”.

The PML-N leader said his party had won in four of the seven territorial constituencies in Muzaffarabad while the PPP, which had been “attempting to build a rigging narrative since 10:30am yesterday”, had secured three.

Sanaullah demanded that the PPP must tell the people how they managed to secure three seats despite the alleged rigging.

“Did they succeed because of rigging or because of a free and fair election?”

Sanaullah further stated that the PML-N had also secured 10 out of 12 refugee seats while the PPP had won two.

“A democratic government, which has the people’s mandate, will now be formed in AJK, and it will work on ideological, economic, and political affairs of the region,” he said.

He added that a parliamentary party session of the PML-N would be called after the conclusion of the third phase of the elections for future decisions.

Speaking about PPP’s rigging allegations, the PML-N leader dismissed them and accused PPP of colluding with the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) to disrupt the election process in Muzaffarabad.

“Anticipating PML-N’s win, PPP along with the action committee planned riots and [..] fired at the police personnel when they got there,” Sanaullah alleged.

He claimed that the incident created an atmosphere of fear in the area, which led to a lower turnout.

“We received at least 3,000 to 4,000 fewer votes due to this,” he claimed.

On PPP’s allegations that an attempt had been made on its candidate AJK Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar’s life, he accused the party of staging a “drama”. He also claimed that the PPP had refused to get Akbar’s medicolegal examination done.

Sanaullah accused the PPP of employing “dirty tricks” to sabotage the electoral process, saying that the PPP’s actions violated the Charter of Democracy, in which the party leadership had agreed that they would not “malign each other’s mandate with such dirty tricks”.

Replying to a question, he said the PPP had raised doubts over “high turnout” in constituencies where the PML-N’s candidate had won.

“With the kind of societal system in place in AJK, it is certainly possible that if there are 300 people in a village, 290 might show up to vote,” he said.

He asked the PPP to follow due process in case of complaints rather than “building a narrative and disrupting democracy and the election process”.

Reports of violence

During the polling on Sunday, attempts were reportedly made to disrupt polling in some neighbourhoods of Muzaffarabad, but voting continued in most areas. In LA-31, Muzaffa­rabad-V (Khawra), clashes between workers of the PML-N and PPP were reported in Union Council Katkair.

The PPP alleged that one of its workers, Syed Mushtaq Shah, was killed in an attack by PML-N supporters. The PML-N rejected the allegation, claiming the man suffered a cardiac arrest following a scuffle between two groups. There was no independent confirmation of either claim.

PPP candidate and Legislative Assembly Speaker Akbar also wrote to the AJK chief election commissioner, alleging security lapses, firing incidents, interference in polling, prevention of polling agents from entering polling stations and denial of voting rights. He also claimed there had been an attempt on his life in which Advocate Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi was injured, and called for an investigation and legal action against those responsible. There was no immediate response from the Election Commission.

Clashes between workers of the two major parties, some involving the use of firearms, were also reported from other areas, though no casualties were immediately reported.

Low turnout outside AJK

Outside AJK, Kashmiris voted for their candidates vying for refugee seats at polling stations set up in Chakwal, Jhelum, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Sialkot, Narowal, Sargodha, Attock, Nawabshah, Hyderabad, Mohmand, Mansehra, Quetta, Dera Ghazi Khan, Peshawar, Sanghar, and Naushahro Feroze.

Polling in these areas largely remained peaceful and recorded a low turnout. In Mohmand, not a single voter turned up at a station set up for the AJK polls. In Dera Ghazi Khan, a single registered female voter cast her ballot at the Govt Elementary School in Maumori, where a polling station had been established just for her.

Out of 12 refugee seats, seven seats are in Punjab, one seat is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, one seat (Jammu-VI) is divided between Pun­jab, Islamabad, and Khyber Pakhtun­khwa, one seat is divided between Sindh and Balo­chistan (Valley-I), and one seat (Jammu-I) is shared among refugees living in Balochistan, Punjab, and Sindh. Valley-V seat is divided between Punjab and Islamabad.

World.title: Iran denies negotiations with US after Trump announces talks
World.content:
Iran said on Monday that no negotiations with the United States were currently being held despite US President Donald Trump announcing earlier that the two sides were set to begin parleys later today.

“Iran is not currently holding talks with the United States and is now in discussions with Oman over a temporary safe route through the Strait of Hormuz,” Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said in a televised press conference.

On Sunday, Trump said that new negotiations with Iran would begin on Monday after he decided to hold off on striking the country to pursue a deal to end the war entering its sixth month.

Trump told reporters that the talks would cover the Strait of Hormuz and ultimately, the denuclearisation of Iran.

Oil prices fell on Monday at the opening of Asian trade after Trump announced the new negotiations, with West Texas Intermediate dropping 4.7 per cent to $80.72 per barrel.

Following a return to strikes last month, fears had mounted that the fighting could escalate once again. Trump had threatened to hit Iran “very hard” and was reportedly considering renewed attacks including against energy infrastructure, with US embassies across the region on alert. Trump pulled back from that threat on Saturday, saying the “parameters” of a deal were there.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, without providing details of the venue or participants in the talks.

The US president said he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on the strikes, which he claimed would have been “the biggest attack since World War II”.

Iranian media denied that Tehran had asked Trump not to strike.

The US president said at the start of the conflict that the war was necessary to deal with Iran’s nuclear programme. Western nations accuse Iran of seeking a bomb, though Tehran insists the programme is entirely civilian in nature.

‘Exchange of views’

Iranian lawmaker Hassan Ghashghavi, spokesman for the parliament’s national security commission, said on Sunday that mediators were trying to revive the US-Iran memorandum of understanding that was agreed in June.

That agreement was not intended as a final peace deal, but as a stepping stone to negotiations on a comprehensive agreement, though it did include provisions on Hormuz.

“They know that the main issue and, in fact, the key to the matter right now is the issue of the Strait of Hormuz, so yes, there is an exchange of views,” Ghashghavi said.

Posting on X, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said, “We must strive to compel the enemy to remain committed to what it has signed.”

Iran deal with Oman?

Before the war, there was free passage for all vessels through the Strait of Hormuz, but Iran closed the strait during the war and now insists on retaining control and charging tolls, something the US rejects.

That dispute sparked the return to strikes last month, as Tehran refused to let ships travel any route other than one which hugs the Iranian coast.

On Sunday, Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Baqaei told state television that a deal was close with Oman, which sits on the other side of the strait, over a new route through it.

“We are now going to reach an understanding on a route acceptable to both sides—neither the northern route nor the southern route — but one that respects the sovereign rights of both sides and safeguards our national interests and security,” he said.

He insisted though that such an agreement did not mean the reopening of the strait.

Baqaei reiterated this during his televised address on Monday, saying that reaching an agreement with Oman was not sufficient to reopen the strait as the situation would remain unchanged while US “aggression” continued.

He elaborated that Iran had been discussing with Oman the creation of a new route through the Strait of Hormuz that would be one path with entry and exit lanes.

The Strait of Hormuz has become a sticking point in the Washington-Tehran conflict, which began with the US and Israel launching strikes on Iran on February 28. Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for 20 per cent of the world’s oil and liquefied natural gas before the start of the war, ​causing energy prices to rise and stoking broader inflation.

Maritime trade tracking firm Kpler said on Friday that traffic through Hormuz had dropped sharply.

On Sunday, a tanker off the coast of Oman reported hearing an explosion near the vessel, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) Centre reported, adding that the vessel and crew were all safe.

World.title: Bulls in charge as PSX opens week by gaining 1,700 points during intraday trade
World.content:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) opened the week in the green, gaining more than 1,700 points during intraday trade.

At 11am, the benchmark KSE-100 index had gained 2273.78 points, from the previous close of 176,094.11 points. By 2:18pm, the index’s gains had dropped to 1781.72 points.

The development came as global oil prices tumbled on Monday as Donald Trump said fresh talks with Iran will begin later in the day.

Mettis Global, a web-based financial portal, said the positive momentum at PSX came as “investors took cues from easing geopolitical tensions after Trump called off a planned strike on Iran, reducing immediate concerns over a wider regional conflict”.

Awais Ashraf, director of research at AKD Securities, said investor optimism extended the positive momentum from the previous week, driven by expectations of a swift agreement between the US and Iran.

“Sentiment improved after the US president announced that talks with Iran would resume on Monday, without setting a deadline for reaching an agreement following the cessation of hostilities,” he said.

Ashraf added that “the return of inflation to single digits in July, with the data due to be released today, would provide an additional catalyst for the market by strengthening expectations of monetary easing and further boosting investor confidence”.

The KSE-100 index ended the first month of the current fiscal year lower. According to Topline Securities Ltd, the index closed July down 4,208 points or 2.3 per cent month-on-month as escalating US-Iran tensions pushed global crude oil prices higher, weighing on investor sentiment.

Average daily traded volume during the month stood at 845 million shares, while average daily traded value was Rs37.5bn.

Additional input from AFP

World.title: Israel conveys 'comments, concerns' to US on Gaza plan, says version made public does not reflect its position
World.content:
Israel has conveyed concerns to the United States on a Gaza plan hailed by President Donald Trump after Hamas said it had agreed on disarmament, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said on Monday.

“Israel has conveyed its comments and concerns on the proposed framework to our American counterparts. The version that has been made public does not reflect Israel’s positions,” Doron Spielman, spokesman for the prime minister’s office, told AFP.
